member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Abstractions.IAuditEntryWriter
member.summary: Application-layer port over the append-only audit trail (ADR-0018, MVP-Data-Dictionary.md §2.22). Implemented in Infrastructure; every mutating action writes through this port, in the same transaction as the state change it describes (mirrors the Outbox pattern's transactional guarantee, ADR-0013), by not calling SaveChanges itself — the caller's own unit-of-work commits both together.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Abstractions.IOutboxWriter
member.summary:
Module-Design.md names IOutboxWriter as one of the Infrastructure module's four public interfaces. This is that port: the only supported way for a business module to say "this happened, and something outside the request must eventually observe it".
Does not save. Like , the implementation adds rows to the caller's own unit of work and leaves the commit to the caller — which is precisely what makes ADR-0013's guarantee hold: the business state change and the Outbox row land in one transaction, or neither lands. A caller that rolls back leaves no Outbox message behind, so a rolled-back operation cannot notify anybody.
Nothing is sent from here. NFR-REL-01: nothing is dispatched from application code inside a request handler. Delivery is the Hangfire dispatcher's job (ADR-0015), after the transaction commits.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Abstractions.IOutboxWriter.WriteAsync(System.String,System.String,System.Guid,System.String,System.DateTime,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Enqueues one event, reserving its ADR-0014 idempotency key (TicketId + EventType + EventVersion) in the same unit of work.
member.returns: The new message, or null when the key is already reserved — meaning this logical event is already enqueued and a second Outbox row must not be written. A duplicate is a normal, expected outcome (a retried request), not an error.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Authorization.AuthorizationGate
member.summary:
The single point through which every application-layer authorization decision in this solution is evaluated, and the one place the is applied to them (ADR-0024 — a confirmed management decision superseding Solution-Analysis.md §4.1's previous exclusion of System Administrator from operational actions).
Why a second mechanism exists at all. Authorization in Tiger CS Ticketing is enforced at two levels, by design: the ASP.NET Core policy catalog (ADR-0005) decides whether a caller may reach an endpoint, and the application services decide the resource-scoped part the policy cannot see — whether this caller may act on this ticket, given its current department and owner (Security-Architecture.md §3: "evaluated against the ticket's current data, not cached or assumed from the user's session alone"). SystemAdministratorOverrideHandler covers the first level for every present and future policy; this gate covers the second for every present and future application service. Together they are the "one central authorization mechanism" of the correction's requirement 4 — the override role itself is defined once, in , and neither level names it inline.
Usage rule. An application service must not branch on the override itself. It passes its own resource-scoped rule to / and uses the answer; the override is applied here, before the rule is consulted (and, for the async overload, without running it — an overridden caller costs no department-membership round trip). A new application service written this way includes the override automatically, which is exactly the property requirement 4 asks for.
What this gate is not. It decides permission only. Everything a service checks that is not a permission — request validation, ticket status-transition rules, closed-ticket immutability, optimistic concurrency, required business data, audit writes — sits outside the gate and is reached unchanged by an overridden caller. Per-record verification-session ownership (MVP-ERD.md §2.24) is deliberately outside it too; see ADR-0024's "Business rules the override does not reach".

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Administration.Services.AdminGenesysRoutingAppService
member.summary:
Administration of the Genesys routing configuration: the Genesys Queue → Department mapping.
Queue → Department, and nothing else. A Genesys queue tells TigerCS which department an inquiry belongs to; it says nothing about what the customer wants. There is deliberately no queue → category mapping and no per-department default category: a ticket whose request nobody has read yet is created Unclassified, and an agent classifies it.
This exists so nothing about routing is hard-coded. Real Genesys queue ids are not known yet, and none are seeded or invented — an administrator enters them here once the Genesys team supplies them, and the integration reads rows. A queue that has not been mapped resolves to no department at all, which ingestion reports as a visible configuration gap rather than papering over with a default.
Mappings are deactivated, never deleted, for the same reason every other configuration table in this system is: an inquiry that arrived under a mapping must stay explainable afterwards.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Abstractions.ICollectionsFinancialSource
member.summary:
The authoritative financial source — the only place a balance comes from.
The source is EDSM, which already has a payment function. Neither the EDSM client nor that function's contract (name, request parameters, response fields, identifier keys) is in this repository, so no EDSM adapter exists yet and none is guessed at: the "Unavailable" provider fails closed on every call and every financial route answers 503. The fixture provider is refused outside Development/Testing. docs/Collections/Collections-Integration.md §2 lists exactly what is needed to write the EDSM adapter behind this port.
An adapter must return the source's own figures: remaining principal per instalment after the source's allocation, penalties and fees with their payable state, applied credits, and posted payments with allocations. A field the source does not provide must surface as invalid/unavailable — never as zero.

AsOf is the first day of the classification month, or - when is set (the By unit view) - TODAY (Dubai), whose CALENDAR MONTH is the reference (CollectionsDueMonth): Overdue = due before the first day of that month, Due = due inside it (any day), anything later is not in scope. PaymentFilter is outstanding, unpaid, partial, paid or all. Status (By unit only) keeps the units that have at least one instalment of that class: overdue or due (null = every unit). MinTotal (By unit): keep units whose summed remaining amount is GREATER than it (null = no minimum).

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Abstractions.IPactCampaignSource
member.summary: A source that evaluates the Campaigns preview/export itself: instalment filtering, per-unit aggregation, the stage amount rule, the unit-level review flags, search, totals and paging all happen in the data store, so only the requested page of units (or, for an export, the bounded full result) reaches the application. A source may answer = false (data not prepared for it); the caller then evaluates in memory.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Abstractions.PactCampaignRequest
member.remarks: The unit's rows are those inside [From, To] (due DAY) with remaining Amount > 0 and >= MinAmount. Stage rows are the ones whose due day is in [StageFrom, StageToExclusive) (StageFrom null = unbounded); a stage amount qualifies when its sum is > Threshold. ContactRequired is false for the internal legal-referral stage. PhoneDigits are the digits of a phone-like search term, else null. Offset/Take page the ordered units (company, tenant, unit code, unit id). Today (Dubai): units carry DueAmount (due inside the month of Today) and OverdueAmount (due before that month); a unit with neither is not a candidate, and MinTotal (null = none) keeps units whose DueAmount + OverdueAmount is greater than it. Units whose code contains '*' (cancelled) are never candidates. [From, To] is the READ scope (it reaches the end of the current month); stage eligibility, the stage amount and the unit flags look at the rows of [eligibility start, To] through the stage window alone (CollectionsCampaignPolicy.StageRange), exactly as the in-memory evaluation and Review do. NOTE: the archived SQL campaign engine (database/collections-receivables/legacy/V007) is built on an older day-based rule, is not deployed and must not be revived without being brought in line with CollectionsDueMonth and this eligibility rule.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Dto.CollectionsPaymentSummaryResponseDto
member.summary:
GET api/collections/customers/by-key/{customerKey}/payment-summary: EDSM's figures for the PACT tenant behind a TigerCS customer, one entry per (companyID, tenantID) pair taken from that tenant's own PACT contracts.
mappingStatus is Mapped or NotMapped. retrievedAtUtc is when TigerCS called EDSM; EDSM returns no as-of time, so sourceAsOfUtc is always null, and figures may lag a posted payment by up to maxSourceDelayMinutes (EDSM's nested caches). currency is configured in TigerCS (currencySource: "Configured"): EDSM returns none. mappingVerifiedAtUtc is when PACT last confirmed the tenant's contracts; mappingSource is PactLookup (discovered on this request), PactLookupPartial (discovered, but PACT did not answer for every phone number, so not cached) or Cached (reused within CollectionsSource:PactMappingTtlMinutes).
completeness says whether the response is the whole picture: Complete (every account and every requested list answered), Partial (something is missing; incompleteReasons says what) or NoFigures (no account has figures: NotMapped, or every company failed). Only a Complete response may be described as the customer's balance. Missing figures are never zero: a company without figures has no fields.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Dto.LinkedUnitCandidateDto
member.summary:
One unit of a customer, linked end to end: the customer (CRM first, PACT completing), the unit (CRM project + apartment, or PACT company + unit code), and the PACT financial result for exactly that unit. Nothing is mixed between candidates: every amount comes from the PACT account of this candidate's company + tenant + unit.
Source: Crm (found through an eligible CRM Sold / Contract sale), Pact (found in PACT by phone, companies 4 / 32) or Leasing (PACT company 7).
LinkStatus: Linked, NeedsReview (see ReviewReasons) or MatchFailed (the unit could not be tied to one PACT unit).
FinancialStatus: Available (amounts), NoDues (PACT confirms nothing is due: a confirmed zero), NoFinancialData (nothing usable: NOT zero), MatchFailed (failed or ambiguous unit / company / project match) or SourceError (a source could not be read). Due / Overdue / Total are null unless Available or NoDues.
FinancialReason: machine-readable cause of anything but Available / NoDues, e.g. ProjectMappingMissing, CompanyMappingAmbiguous, PactHoldsNoRecord, CompanySnapshotNotLoaded, LeasingReceivablesSourceMissing, PactUnavailable.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Dto.UnitPaymentStatementDto
member.summary: The complete payment statement of ONE unit: Due | Outstanding | Paid | Fines | Total, then Payment Details (Date | Status | Amount | Cheque Number) with paid, unpaid and future rows. Source: PACT's EDSM payment summary / transactions of the unit's (company, tenant) account - the same source as the CRM "Pact Payment" screen. EDSM aggregates per account, so the statement is shown ONLY when PACT's contract list proves that the account belongs exclusively to this unit; otherwise Status says why and no amount is shown. Status: Available; AmountsUnreadable (EDSM answered but no figure could be read: number format not configured); NotExclusive (the account also covers OtherUnits); UnitNotFound (PACT lists no active contract for this unit under the customer's phone numbers); Ambiguous (several accounts claim the unit); IdentityMismatch; ContractEnded; Unverified (PACT could not be fully read, so exclusivity cannot be proven); CompanyNotSupported; NotConfigured; SourceUnavailable; UnitNotResolved (no PACT unit code yet). Nothing here is ever derived from the Due / Overdue collections snapshot.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Reconciliation.FinancialReconciliationService
member.summary: Reconciles the local receivables snapshot (what the pages show and what an approval is built from) with a FRESH, direct read of the same configured PACT procedure, per company, unit by unit and instalment by instalment (). It is started only on request (never by a page view), one at a time, with a cooldown. A run that cannot complete (PACT unreachable, snapshot not fresh, snapshot republished during the run) is an Error - missing evidence, never a "pass" and never a finding. BASIS (): both sides are the output of the SAME PACT procedure (the snapshot via the refresh job's linked-server call, the other side via a direct call), so this is a SNAPSHOT-CONSISTENCY check, not an independent ledger reconciliation. It never sets or implies the human sign-off, which remains mandatory in .

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Reconciliation.ReconciliationBasis
member.summary: What the automated reconciliation compares and, just as important, what it does NOT establish. Both sides are the output of the SAME PACT procedure: the snapshot is that procedure's result copied by the refresh job (linked server), the other side is that procedure called again over a direct connection. Agreement therefore proves the snapshot is a faithful, current copy; it does not prove the procedure's figures are right against PACT's ledger. That is only ever attested by the recorded human sign-off.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Review.CurrentBalanceReader
member.summary:
Re-reads current balances for the companies involved in a dispatch or a suppression sweep and rebuilds the review records, keyed by RecordKey. One read per company, run concurrently (they hit different PACT databases).
Source limitation. The PACT report procedures accept only @StartDate, @EndDate and @MinAmount (V2 adds @IncludeSettled and @StrictIdentity); none selects a customer, unit or tag, and the ledger and allocation work runs in full whatever the window. The window cannot be narrowed safely either: a unit's quoted amount sums every qualifying instalment from the configured start date, and an older instalment that becomes unpaid again (a reversed cheque) would be missed. So the cost of one revalidation is one full company read, which is why it runs in the background job with a lease heartbeat. Targeted reads need a new, separately reviewed procedure parameter; none is invented here.
Same filters as the preview. The read uses the same minimum outstanding amount (DefaultMinOutstandingAmount, remaining >= value per instalment), the same configured start date and, with the local snapshot, the same rows as the Campaigns preview and export, and requires the snapshot to be fresh and to cover the window.

member.summary:
Approval and upload of reviewed records to Genesys outbound contact lists.
Confirm: authorizes, re-resolves the approved list and refuses it if it differs from what was shown, then stores a frozen dispatch (idempotent by key; each record can be in only one live dispatch) and queues a job.
Execute (job): takes a lease, re-reads the current balances, excludes settled records, stops for review on any other change, then uploads one batch per reminder type (at most 1,000 contacts each). A batch whose outcome is unknown is never re-sent; it waits for reconciliation.
"Uploaded to Genesys" means the contact is in the list. It never means the customer was called or contacted.

member.summary: Runs slow, database-free work (the PACT reads) while renewing the lease on a timer, so a read that outlasts the lease cannot let a second worker start. The timer only touches the store while the work awaits the source, and is stopped (awaited) before the caller uses the store again. If the lease cannot be renewed the work is cancelled and is thrown.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Review.DispatchService.CampaignGates
member.summary: Resolves the Genesys campaign named exactly like the batch's stage before any contact is uploaded. An existing campaign with that name is reused (never duplicated) when it dials this batch's contact list; a missing one is created when allowed. Anything uncertain (several matches, a different contact list, an unusable template, a failed or unanswered Genesys call) fails the batch with nothing uploaded; the records are released, and a later send looks the campaign up again first, so an unconfirmed creation can never produce a duplicate. Returns false when the batch was failed.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Review.DispatchService.EnsureCampaignAsync(TigerCS.Domain.Modules.Collections.Review.CollectionsDispatch,TigerCS.Domain.Modules.Collections.Review.CollectionsGenesysBatch,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: "Look up, then create" is not atomic in Genesys, so two dispatches of the same stage working at once could both find nothing and both create the campaign. Lookup and creation therefore run one at a time per campaign name inside this process (the second waits, then finds the first one's campaign and reuses it). Several API instances would need Genesys's own unique-name rule as the backstop - it refuses a second campaign with the same name, which the batch then reports as not created.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Review.SuppressionService
member.summary:
Paid-after-upload protection. An uploaded contact stays in the Genesys list until someone removes it, so a customer who pays after the upload could still be called. This sweep re-reads current balances and, for every uploaded contact whose balance was paid or changed, sets the Genesys contact callable=false (documented "Update a contact": PUT /api/v2/outbound/contactlists/{contactListId}/contacts/{contactId}). Deleting is not used: the documented bulk delete only removes contacts not in use by a campaign.
Limits (cannot be removed in code). A call already dialled or connected cannot be recalled; a contact a running campaign has already pulled into its dialling queue may be dialled before the next sweep; the sweep interval, the PACT read time and Genesys rate limits all add delay. Whether Genesys honours callable=false for a contact already queued by an active campaign has to be proven on a test list before live use.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Services.CollectionsNextPaymentService
member.summary:
The next-payment answer for a PACT-identified customer's mapped EDSM companies (docs/Collections/Next-Payment.md). It reads EDSM's v1/due-installments — the only EDSM route with instalment-level dated rows — only for a company whose semantics the EDSM owners have confirmed in (docs/Collections/EDSM-Instalment-Semantics.md). Anything unconfirmed is an explicit Unavailable with reasons, and EDSM is not called for it.
Search. Forward from the business date in WindowDays-day windows (consecutive windows overlap by one day, and rows are de-duplicated, so an inclusive/exclusive range boundary cannot hide a row) through SearchHorizonDays, stopping at the first window that holds an unpaid instalment — the earliest unpaid date is then the earliest overall, because windows are visited in date order. It never silently stops at a fixed 31 days: the horizon is configured, and reported as searchedThrough.
Never infers. A row is a candidate only if its raw status is in the attested unpaid set, its chequeDueDate is present, and its amount is present and positive. Overdue (due today or earlier) is excluded by .

Sends one queued SMS/email channel — after re-reading the account from the financial source immediately before delivery. A settled, ineligible, stale-read or inconsistent account is suppressed instead of reminded, and the amount re-read is stored next to the amount quoted.
Runs on the existing outbox dispatcher, so retries, attempt limits and dead-lettering are the platform's, and two workers never send the same message twice (the outbox claim). Provider acceptance is Sent; Delivered comes only from the provider's own report.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Services.CollectionsPaymentSummaryAppService
member.summary:
EDSM's figures for a TigerCS customer (docs/Collections/EDSM_Collections_Contract.md).
Account resolution. EDSM keys every route by the (companyID, tenantID) pair. It answers an unknown tenant with 200 and zeros, so an EDSM response never proves that an account exists. Existence and ownership come only from PACT's v1/contracts/{mobile}:
TigerCS persists a PACT customer as ext:Pact:{tenantID}.
The customer's phone numbers are looked up in PACT, and only rows whose own tenantID equals the stored tenant are kept. Each pair is taken from the same row, and the tenant id always comes from tenantID, never from a unit or contract reference. For Parking units, UserUnit.RefId is the ContractID, so it is never used.
EDSM is asked only for those pairs: one summary per company, with that company's contracts listed.
Directory reads retain their stored identity. Pre-ticket lookup reads may associate CRM and PACT only through CustomerIdentityLinker's fresh, unambiguous evidence; this is not a persisted CRM-to-PACT crosswalk.
Field definitions differ for owned companies (4, 32) and rented companies (25, 7, 20). They are mapped separately, from EDSM's C# code. TigerCS shows EDSM's figures; it never recomputes, adds or nets them, and none of them feed reminder eligibility.
Side effect, accepted knowingly: PACT's v1/contracts/{mobile} writes customer-type and UserUnit rows in EDSM (contract §8.3). TigerCS's existing customer lookup already makes this call. This service adds one per Payment tab load and phone number.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Collections.Services.CollectionsReminderAppService
member.summary:
Reminder candidates and the queue.
Candidate first. A reminder can only be queued from a candidate — an eligible account, its qualifying instalments and amount, computed from a fresh, non-stale source read. Queueing re-reads the account and accepts the candidate only if it is unexpired and a fresh evaluation reproduces it exactly; otherwise 409 CandidateChanged with a replacement. No client ever supplies a balance or a destination.
No duplicates. Each channel's account | type | cycle | channel key is unique in the database; an Idempotency-Key replays the original job (or conflicts when reused with a different body) and never bypasses cycle de-duplication. Only a failed channel may be retried, within its attempt budget.

Delivery events and customer responses reported for a reminder.
Idempotent. (reminder, eventId) is unique. A resend with the same body returns the original result; the same eventId or Idempotency-Key with a different body is 409 IdempotencyConflict. Delivery statuses are validated per channel and applied in occurrence order, so a delayed event never overwrites a later or final status.
A customer response in a conversation gets a ticket through the existing Genesys ingestion — , keyed by conversationId, routed by the configured Collections queue or department code, created Unclassified under the existing classification and lifecycle rules. AlreadyPaid requests verification and posts nothing; a human request, an AI disconnection, a dispute or an explicit requiresHumanFollowUp keeps human work outstanding through the existing handoff. Nothing here resolves or closes a ticket.
Durable. The event and an outbox message commit together before the ticket is attempted; if the ticket cannot be created yet the answer is 202 with ticketResult: "Pending", and the outbox retries ().

The complete payment statement of ONE unit (Due | Outstanding | Paid | Fines | Total, and the payment rows), from the authoritative PACT source the CRM "Pact Payment" screen uses: EDSM's payment summary and payment transactions () - never from the Due / Overdue collections snapshot, which holds unpaid remainders only.
Unit isolation. EDSM aggregates per (company, tenant), not per unit (EDSM contract: "granularity UNVERIFIED"), so it has no unit-scoped route. The statement is shown ONLY when PACT's own contract list (v1/contracts/{mobile}, which returns ALL of a tenant's contracts / units) proves that the (company, tenant) account has exactly one unit: the selected one. Another unit, a parking contract, an ended or cancelled contract of the same tenant, a contract without a unit code, or an incomplete PACT answer all withhold the amounts and say why: another unit's money is never shown, and a missing figure is never shown as zero.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.Abstractions.ICrmDocumentGateway
member.summary:
Tiger CRM's customer-document source — POST {Crm}/TicketingSystem/GetCustomerDocuments — and the authorized retrieval of the files it points at.
Documents are addressed by CRM's own CustomerID + LeadID (the customer and the selected unit), obtained from the verified customer's CRM buyer lookup — never from the caller. The gateway promises that what it returns is what CRM said for that customer and lead: a response that names a different customer or lead is refused as an invalid response.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.CrmDocumentOptions
member.summary: Settings for the chatbot's "send me a copy of my document" API, bound from CrmDocuments. A plain Application-layer value (the composition root binds it), like GenesysOptions.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.CrmDocumentOptions.Enabled
member.summary: The feature flag. False (the default) answers 503 DOCUMENT_COPY_DISABLED and touches nothing.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.CrmDocumentOptions.AcceptedVerificationMethods
member.summary: Verification methods accepted as proof of identity for a chatbot document request. Default: a one-time code, or an authenticated digital user. ManualAgentConfirmation is deliberately absent — an agent ticking a box is not something a bot channel should lean on to release contracts — and so is any method a caller could assert on its own.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.CrmDocumentOptions.AgentSendRoles
member.summary: Roles granted the agent desk's Send to customer (Customer Details → Documents). This is a separate grant from being able to see the customer or open their files: a role not listed can do both of those and still cannot send. The System Administrator override (ADR-0024) applies as everywhere else. Unset (null) means the shipped default (); when configured the list replaces the default (the configuration binder would otherwise append to it and a role could never be taken away).

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.CrmDocumentOptions.EffectiveAgentSendRoles
member.summary: The roles that hold the send grant, after applying the default.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.CrmDocumentOptions.MaxAttachmentBytes
member.summary: Largest document sent as an attachment. Bigger answers DELIVERY_FAILED/DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE rather than risking a mailbox rejection.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.CrmDocumentOptions.InProgressStaleAfterMinutes
member.summary: An unfinished send older than this is treated as abandoned and may be retaken by a retry.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.CrmDocumentOptions.PostSendSaveAttempts
member.summary: How many times the "Sent" record is saved after the provider has accepted the email. The email cannot be taken back, so the save is retried rather than abandoned; if every attempt fails the request is left Dispatching and answers "unconfirmed".

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.CrmDocumentOptions.PostSendSaveRetryDelayMilliseconds
member.summary: Pause before the n-th retry of that save is n × this many milliseconds.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.CrmDocumentOptions.DuplicateSuppressionMinutes
member.summary: The same document, session and channel is not sent again within this window even under a new idempotency key.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.Dto.CrmDocumentCopyRequestDto.ConversationId
member.summary: Optional. The Genesys conversation this request belongs to. When sent it names the ticket whose document workflow the outcome closes (Sent → closed as resolved; a delivery failure → closed with the failure reason). Omitted, the ticket that consumed the verification session is used, if any; with neither, no ticket is touched.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.Dto.CrmDocumentCopyRequestDto.ServiceRequestId
member.summary: Optional. Which service request of the conversation this document request fulfils (the same serviceRequestId the ticket was created with). When a conversation carries several tickets this is what makes the outcome close the documents ticket and never a sibling (for example an apartment-leasing ticket). Omitted, the conversation's default (first) ticket is used, as before. A ticket that needs human follow-up is never closed by a document outcome, whichever way it was found.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.Services.CrmBuyerVerificationCache
member.summary:
Fills the verification unit/contact cache (UnitReferences / ContactReferences) from the real CRM buyer lookup (GetBuyerByPhone) — the one CRM operation that exists — so a verification session has the rows it refers to.
Mapping, from existing buyer-lookup fields only:
Unit — CrmUnitId = String(unitId) (the same id the document flow matches on), UnitNumber = unitNumber, PropertyName = projectName. Tower and unit-type label stay null: the buyer lookup has neither (unitType is a bare numeric code).
Contact — CrmContactId = "{customerId}-{unitId}": unit-scoped, because CrmContactId is globally unique and a contact row belongs to one unit, so one customer on two units needs two rows. Name from fullNameEnglish/fullNameArabic, channel from mobileNumber (the searched number when CRM returns none).
Contact type — , recorded as CRM labels it. customerType = 1 is not turned into : its ownership meaning is unconfirmed.
The customer, unit and lead relationship is not lost to the cache's shape: the OTP challenge and the session it produces carry CRM's customer id and lead id (see ).
Existing agent-desk rows are never degraded. A unit already cached by the unit/contact lookup keeps its tower and unit type; a contact row that already exists with another type keeps that type.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.Services.CrmDocumentCopyAppService
member.summary:
"Send me a copy of my contract / reservation form / unit layout / registration receipt" — the chatbot's request, answered end to end.
Identity is proven, not asserted. The only identity input is a from the existing verification flow: it must be owned by the calling integration account, confirmed (or already consumed by a ticket), unexpired, and verified by a method this API accepts ( — a one-time code or an authenticated digital user by default). A phone number or a customer id is not even a field of the request.
Who CRM is asked about. The verified session's contact (on record in CRM, never the caller) gives the phone for the existing CRM buyer lookup; that returns CRM's CustomerID and the customer's units with their LeadIDs. The lead is the verified unit, or one the caller names that must be among that customer's units — anything else is an ownership mismatch and CRM is never asked. GetCustomerDocuments is then called with exactly that CustomerID/LeadID.
Ownership is enforced at every step. The lead belongs to the customer (above); CRM must echo that customer and lead back (the gateway refuses a response that does not); a recordId the caller names must be one CRM just listed for them — never fetched otherwise, so a guessed id cannot retrieve another customer's document; and the file is fetched with the server-side CRM credential from the reference in that same listing, never from anything the caller supplied.
Never an arbitrary document. Several matching records → the choices are returned and nothing is sent; the chatbot asks the customer and calls again with recordId.
Never twice. The caller's idempotency key claims the send in a unique-indexed row before anything is fetched or sent. A replay of a sent request answers Sent without sending; a concurrent replay answers Queued; a failed one may be retried; the same key with a different request is refused. A retry under a new key within is caught by the second check (same session, document, channel) and also sends nothing.
Private. The document travels as an attachment to the customer's own email address as held by CRM — no link, so there is nothing to expire or leak — and is never stored or logged here.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.Services.CrmDocumentCopyAppService.IdempotencyKeyPattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[A-Za-z0-9._:\\-]{1,128}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [\-.0-:A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 1 and at most 128 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[^@\\s]+@[^@\\s]+\\.[^@\\s]+$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [^@\s] atomically at least once.
○ Match '@'.
○ Match a character in the set [^@\s] greedily at least once.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [^@\s] atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.summary:
The agent desk's "Send to customer": the same delivery core as the chatbot (record chosen only from CRM's own listing for this customer and lead, idempotency claim, server-side download, one email attachment to CRM's address for the customer, audit) — but the proof of who the customer is comes from the signed-in agent's access to that customer, established by , instead of a customer OTP.
The agent cannot choose the destination: it is CRM's email for the customer. The delivery record is explicit about its origin (): it carries the CRM customer and lead, and its verification session reference stays null — nothing is invented to fill a column meant for a real session. The idempotency key, the replay rules and the 15-minute "same document already sent" suppression all work on that customer + lead scope.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.Services.CustomerDocumentsAppService
member.summary:
The Customer Details Documents tab: the customer's Reservation Form (CRM type 4), Tiger Contract (5) and Registration Receipt (6) for the selected unit, the file behind each, and "Send to customer".
No parallel integration. Documents come from the existing (TicketingSystem/GetCustomerDocuments and the credentialed file fetch); the customer and unit from the existing ; sending is — the very service behind /api/genesys/documents/send-copy.
Ownership, in order, on every call. (1) The customer must be visible to the signed-in agent — the same department-scoped check as the Customer Profile itself, so a customer key the agent cannot open yields nothing. (2) It must be a CRM customer, and CRM must resolve one of the phones TigerCS holds for them to that same CRM customer. (3) The unit (crmLeadId) must be one of that customer's CRM units — a lead id typed into the URL is checked, never trusted. (4) A file or send names a record only if CRM has just listed it for that customer, unit and type; CRM's storage reference never leaves the server, and the gateway refuses a listing that echoes another customer or lead.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.Services.CustomerOtpAppService
member.summary:
Real customer verification for a CRM buyer reaching TigerCS through the chatbot: look the buyer up in CRM → pick a unit → email a one-time code to the address CRM holds → check the code on the server → create the OTP-verified session.
The code is the proof; nothing the caller says is. The phone number the chatbot sends is only the key CRM is searched by. The destination is always the email CRM returns for that customer — no request has a destination field. A session with verificationMethod: Otp can only come out of ; the generic session endpoint refuses that method, and the document flow refuses any session that lacks the recorded challenge.
Bound at creation: the integration account, CRM's customer, the selected unit and its lead. Verification by another account, or for another customer or unit, is impossible — the challenge is looked up by id and account, and the session is built from the challenge's own binding.
Limits (all configurable, CrmDocuments:Otp*): a code lives 10 minutes; 5 wrong tries lock the challenge for good; at most 3 sends per challenge with 60 s between them (a resend replaces the code); at most 5 challenges per customer per hour from any caller; a repeated "send" for a live challenge does not email again. The code is stored only as a salted HMAC and compared in constant time; wrong-try and single-use accounting use concurrency tokens so parallel guesses cannot dodge the budget.
Disclosure note: the lookup returns the customer's unit labels (project and unit number) before proof, so the customer can choose which unit to verify for — the same information the existing Genesys customer lookup already returns to the call flow. It never returns the customer's name, phone, CRM ids beyond unit/lead, or the full email.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.Services.DocumentDeliveryTicketService
member.summary:
Closes — through the existing lifecycle (Resolved → Closed, audit, history, Outbox) — the ticket behind a Genesys document request, once the request's workflow has ended.
Which ticket. Only one the existing associations name: the ticket of the Genesys conversation the chatbot sent (conversationId → its interaction), else the ticket that consumed the verification session. It must still be open, belong to the same CRM customer when it has one, and — for a conversation — have been started from the verified contact's phone number. Anything else is left alone: this never searches for "a ticket of this customer". When the conversation carries several tickets, the request's serviceRequestId picks the right one, and a ticket that is human follow-up (flagged by Genesys, or with an open handoff) is never closed by a document outcome.
When. Sent closes as Resolved with the fixed reason; a failure closes as Cancelled with "Document delivery failed — [actual reason]" and the code, document type and time in the history/audit. Both wait while another request of the same verification session is still being processed. An unconfirmed outcome never closes anything and is never described as success or failure — it is recorded on the ticket for a person. A failed ticket is never transferred. Re-running on a closed ticket changes nothing. Failures here never reach the caller: the document has already been dealt with.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.VerificationTestingPolicy
member.summary:
Decides, at the outbound delivery layer, where an OTP or document message really goes.
Test mode off (the default, and the only state Production can be in): every route is the customer's own contact detail, unchanged. Test mode on: every route is the configured override — and if the configuration is invalid, incomplete or enabled in a non-allowed environment, is true and nothing is routable, so a real customer can never be messaged by a half-configured test mode. There is no fallback to the real address.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.VerificationTestingPolicy.EmailPattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[^@\\s]+@[^@\\s]+\\.[^@\\s]+$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [^@\s] atomically at least once.
○ Match '@'.
○ Match a character in the set [^@\s] greedily at least once.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [^@\s] atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CrmDocuments.VerificationTestingPolicy.SmsPattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[1-9]\\d{7,14}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [1-9].
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least 7 and at most 14 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerReviews.Services.TicketReviewAppService
member.summary:
The server side of the public review page. Reached without a login, so the token is the only credential and every decision is made here: the page and the email links are never trusted.
Looking at a link changes nothing. is read-only — email security scanners and link previews that open the rating links cannot submit a review.
Submitting is explicit and once. The review is committed only by ; the unique index on ticket cycle makes a second or simultaneous submission fail without touching the first.
Bad tokens look alike. Malformed, unknown and altered tokens all answer Invalid.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerReviews.Services.TicketReviewInvitationService
member.summary:
Issues the secure review links that go into Resolved and Closed emails.
A link is issued only when the customer has not already reviewed this ticket cycle — so the Closed email never asks again after a review was given, and an existing review is never put at risk — and only when a public base URL is configured to build the link from. Otherwise the email is sent without a review section.
Staged, not saved: the notification dispatcher commits the invitation together with the delivery record. A retried delivery therefore issues a fresh link; earlier unused ones simply expire, and either can submit the one review.

Issues the secure review links that go into Resolved and Closed emails.
A link is issued only when the customer has not already reviewed this ticket cycle — so the Closed email never asks again after a review was given, and an existing review is never put at risk — and only when a public base URL is configured to build the link from. Otherwise the email is sent without a review section.
Staged, not saved: the notification dispatcher commits the invitation together with the delivery record. A retried delivery therefore issues a fresh link; earlier unused ones simply expire, and either can submit the one review.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.Abstractions.DuplicateWriteException
member.summary: Thrown by when a save fails because it violated a real DB-level uniqueness constraint — two concurrent requests racing to create a VerificationSessions row with the same (AgentEmployeeId, IdempotencyKey) pair (VerificationSessionAppService), or two concurrent lookups racing to cache the same never-before-seen UnitReferences.CrmUnitId / ContactReferences.CrmContactId (CrmUnitLookupAppService). Deliberately narrower than "any failed save": the Infrastructure-layer translation (CustomerVerificationUnitOfWork) only raises this for an actual unique-constraint/duplicate-key violation, never for an unrelated database update failure (a foreign-key violation, a required-field violation, a genuine connectivity failure), which every caller of this exception must be able to rely on before treating it as safely recoverable-by-requery. Translated from the concrete EF Core exception in Infrastructure so the Application layer never depends on EF Core types directly.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.CrmIntegration.ICrmBuyerLookupGateway
member.summary:
Tiger CRM's real, manually-verified GET /TicketingSystem/GetBuyerByPhone endpoint — a second, narrow read-only CRM port alongside (unit-number lookup) and ICrmCustomerLookupGateway (generic CRM/PACT/Tasleeh phone enrichment). This one is Buyer-specific: it returns every matching CRM customer plus the units each owns whose Lead is Sold or Contract, exactly as Tiger CRM itself already filters (MVP-Implementation-Backlog.md's CRM Buyer Lookup increment).
Read-only, and never resolves ambiguity on its own. This is the raw CRM contract boundary — it returns CRM's response exactly as CRM sent it, including the (expected-never-to-happen) case of more than one customer entry for one phone number. Business rule: CRM guarantees a phone number belongs to exactly one customer; enforcing/consolidating that (and staying resilient if CRM's own response does not honor it) is CrmBuyerLookupAppService's job, not this port's — this interface stays a thin, unopinionated passthrough. One customer may still own multiple valid units, and this port picks none of them: no automatic unit selection, matching the business rule that only the CS agent (via the New Ticket UI) may choose the relevant unit. This interface holds no verification state and makes no ticket-creation decision, matching every other CRM port's own documented boundary.
Implemented in TigerCS.Integrations.Modules.CrmIntegration (CrmBuyerHttpGateway) as a real HTTP-backed gateway — unlike /ICrmCustomerLookupGateway, no Mock implementation exists for this port: the CRM endpoint it calls has already been implemented and manually verified CRM-side, so this is a genuine integration from the start.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.CrmIntegration.ICrmGateway
member.summary:
The Tiger Group CRM's entire responsibility toward this system, and the only thing this interface may ever grow to do: read-only data access. Tiger CRM (i) looks up a unit by unit number, (ii) returns that unit's immutable CRM-issued identifier plus the minimum display details needed for an agent's verbal read-back, and (iii) returns the contacts/owners/tenants/authorized representatives linked to that unit. Nothing more.
This is a data-access integration port, not a verification authority. It holds no state machine, no session concept, no eligibility rule, no audit trail, and makes no decision about whether a ticket may be created — those are all Tiger CS Ticketing's own business logic (VerificationSessionAppService: selecting the requester, recording the verification method/result, deciding whether ticket creation is allowed, capturing the immutable verification-time snapshot, and the audit/authorization/expiry rules around all of it).
is this port's only caller — it does cache-aside lookups against this interface and nothing else; it is not where verification decisions are made either.
Implemented in TigerCS.Integrations.Modules.CrmIntegration — either a real HTTP-backed gateway, or the feature-flagged mock adapter used while real CRM endpoint details are unavailable (never described as production-ready — see MockCrmGateway). Any future automated intake surface (e.g. a Genesys AI voice/chat integration) that needs a unit or contact looked up must call Tiger CS Ticketing's own API — it must never call this interface, or any CRM system, directly: verification rules and the decision of whether a ticket may be created live only in Tiger CS Ticketing, and only Tiger CS Ticketing is a legitimate caller of a CRM data source.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.CustomerLookup.ICrmCustomerLookupGateway
member.summary:
Business-rule change: customer lookup is enrichment/identification, not a Ticket creation gate. Each of the three external sources — Tiger CRM, PACT, and Tasleeh — gets its own narrow, read-only, phone-search-only port, deliberately separate from ICrmGateway (that interface's own remarks scope it to unit-number lookup only; phone-based customer search is a different capability with a different caller, CustomerLookupAppService, and must never be able to widen ICrmGateway's own documented boundary).
Every implementation must fail closed, never block. A source that cannot be reached throws its own *GatewayUnavailableException (or, for PACT's outcome-wrapped port, returns a non-Success outcome); CustomerLookupAppService handles each source independently so one source's outage never affects another's result, and none of the three ever prevents a ticket from being created.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.PactIntegration.IPactCustomerLookupGateway
member.summary:
PACT's real customer/contract lookup by mobile number — the PACT counterpart of , and the port CustomerLookupAppService's PACT leg searches when a Department's DepartmentCustomerLookupSource configuration enables the Pact source. Backed by PACT's GET v1/contracts/{mobile} (the customer's contracts/units) and GET v1/contracts/{mobile}/customer-type (the customer's PACT-recorded type, fetched only when the contracts response did not already carry one).
Read-only, and never resolves ambiguity on its own. Returns every matched customer (0..N) with every contract/unit PACT associates with them (0..N) — no automatic selection of a first result, matching the business rule that only the CS agent may choose the relevant customer/ unit. PACT has no local UnitReference/ContactReference cache table, so a PACT contract is display enrichment for the agent, never linked to a Ticket by id.
Every failure mode maps to a outcome — implementations never throw for an expected PACT response (mirrors 's own contract): PACT being down, misconfigured, or answering garbage all collapse to a non-Success outcome, which CustomerLookupAppService reports as a Failed source alongside the other sources' results — a PACT failure or empty answer never blocks New Ticket creation, and the agent can always fall back to manual customer/unit entry.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.PactIntegration.PactCustomerLookupOutcome
member.summary: Every outcome can return — same shape as .

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.PactIntegration.PactCustomerLookupOutcome.Success
member.summary: PACT answered with at least one matching customer (each carrying 0..N contracts/units).

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.PactIntegration.PactCustomerLookupOutcome.NotFound
member.summary: PACT answered and has no customer on file for this mobile number (404, or a 200 body with no match).

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.PactIntegration.PactCustomerLookupOutcome.Unauthorized
member.summary: PACT rejected the request's X-API-KEY (401/403) — a configuration problem, not a data-not-found result.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.PactIntegration.PactCustomerLookupOutcome.InvalidResponse
member.summary: PACT answered 200 with a body that does not parse as the documented contract, or answered 400.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.PactIntegration.PactCustomerLookupOutcome.Unavailable
member.summary: PACT could not be reached at all — timeout, network failure, missing configuration, a server error, or an unexpected HTTP status.

member.param: PACT's own identifier for the customer (its tenant id). Never a local reference id — PACT has no local cache table.
The customer's name, when PACT has one on file.
The customer's mobile number, when PACT echoes one back.
The customer's email, when PACT has one on file.

PACT's raw customer-type value — for the real HTTP gateway this is the numeric customerBuyerType CODE as a string (e.g. "1"/"2"; PACT's code table is not published), taken from the contracts response when it carries one, otherwise from GET v1/contracts/{mobile}/customer-type; null when neither has it. Not display text: no UI may present this raw code as a customer-type label until the PACT code table is confirmed and translated.
Every contract/unit (0..N) PACT associates with this customer — never assumed to be exactly one, and never auto-selected.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.PactIntegration.PactContractActivity
member.summary:
The one rule for whether a PACT contract is still current: a contract whose falls before today's Dubai calendar date has expired; one ending today or later is active.
"Today" is the Dubai calendar date, never the server's. PACT's dates are UAE business dates, and the API may run on a UTC host where, between 20:00 and midnight UTC, the server date is still "yesterday" in Dubai — a contract ending on that Dubai date must already count as active-today, not as tomorrow's. is the single place that conversion happens for PACT contract filtering.
A missing or unreadable date never hides a contract. The gateway leaves ContractEndDate null for an absent or malformed PACT value (see PactContractDateParser); treating that as "expired" would hide real, current contracts over a formatting quirk, so a null is always active — the agent sees it exactly as before this rule existed.
The lookup layer marks expired contracts but retains them. New Ticket applies this rule when offering selectable units, while the Collections account mapping (which needs every contract, expired or not, to resolve a tenant's EDSM accounts) and persisted ticket history keep reading the gateway unfiltered.

member.summary: Today's calendar date in Dubai, taken from 's UTC clock.

member.summary: True when the contract is still current on : it ends today or later, or carries no readable end date at all. Only an end date strictly before expires it.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.Services.CrmBuyerLookupAppService
member.summary:
The only caller of — searches Tiger CRM by phone number for Buyer records. CRM's own endpoint is the source of truth for which units are Sold/Contract-eligible: real CRM Lead status codes are not a small, stable, closed set Ticketing can safely hard-code (e.g. status 4 = "Contract" in production, not just 8/9 as an earlier, pre-launch assumption had it), so this service does not re-filter by at all — whatever CRM returns as a match, Ticketing accepts. The one check retained is 's CustomerType == Buyer: this phase supports Buyer matches only, and that is a Ticketing-side scoping decision, not a guess at CRM's own status semantics.
Business rule: a CRM phone number belongs to exactly one customer. CRM guarantees phone-number uniqueness per customer, so this service always resolves to at most one — never a list of distinct customers for the caller to disambiguate. A customer may still own multiple valid units, and every one of them is returned, unfiltered beyond the Buyer check above. A customer left with zero valid units after filtering is dropped entirely; a lookup left with zero customers after that becomes , even though CRM itself answered .
Never guesses when CRM breaks its own uniqueness guarantee. CRM naming the same CustomerId more than once is not a distinct-customer situation — merges those entries' units (deduplicated by UnitId) into one . But CRM naming two or more genuinely different CustomerIds for the same phone number is a real data-integrity conflict this service refuses to paper over: it does not pick a "first" customer, does not return a result at all, and never lets a Ticket or IntakeRecord get linked to either candidate automatically. Instead it returns and logs one warning for investigation — the phone number masked and the distinct CustomerIds named, but never CRM's secret key (this service never has it in the first place; see CrmBuyerHttpGateway). This service never throws for this case either.
No local reference/cache table exists for Buyer matches (see 's remarks) — this phase does not copy CRM master data into Ticketing; a future ticket-creation flow stores only the CRM identifiers plus an immutable ticket-time snapshot, not a synchronized copy of CRM's own customer/unit tables.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.Services.CrmUnitLookupAppService
member.summary:
MVP-API-Contracts.md §2.1-§2.3 — CRM unit/contact lookup only, cache-aside against 's read-only data-access port (ADR-0006): every lookup upserts the local UnitReferences/ ContactReferences display cache from the CRM's response, never treating the cache itself as authoritative. This service makes no verification decision — it does not select a requester, does not record a verification result, and does not decide whether ticket creation may proceed. Those are 's responsibility (Tiger CS Ticketing business logic, not CRM business logic — see that type's remarks); this service exists only to give it (and the API's CRM-lookup endpoints) something to select from.
Refresh/staleness. There is no TTL-based expiry — every lookup through this service (, , ) is a synchronous read-through: it always calls first and overwrites the cache row with whatever the CRM returns (UnitReference.RefreshFromCrm/ ContactReference.RefreshFromCrm), then serves the caller the just-refreshed data. The cache therefore can only be as stale as "however long ago this exact unit/contact was last looked up" — surfaced to every caller via LastSyncedAtUtc so staleness is never silent. Nothing in this module reads the cache without going through the gateway first (no cache-only lookup path exists).
Data minimization. Both cache tables and every response DTO in this module carry only the fields FR-VER-01–04's verify-then-create workflow actually needs for read-back/identification: unit number/property/tower/type, and per-contact display name/channel/type/ representative-authorization link. No other CRM field is ever requested, cached, or returned. (unit lookup/search) deliberately carries no contact-level data at all — only a ContactCount — so a unit search never leaks a customer's name, contact channel, or contact type; that PII is returned only from the dedicated, unit-scoped call, which FR-VER-04 requires so the agent can identify which specific contact is on the line.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.Services.CrmUnitLookupAppService.UpsertUnitAsync(TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.CrmIntegration.CrmUnitResult,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Find-or-create against UnitReferences.CrmUnitId (the correct, immutable CRM external identifier — MVP-Data-Dictionary.md §2.7 — enforced by a real DB-level unique index, UnitReferenceConfiguration). The find-then-insert here is still a TOCTOU race on its own (two concurrent lookups of the same never-before-cached unit can both find nothing and both attempt to insert); the unique index is the actual backstop, and this method safely recovers from it: attempt the write, and on — a genuine unique-constraint violation only, never an unrelated database update failure, see CustomerVerificationUnitOfWork's remarks — reload and return the winner's row instead of a second, orphaned local instance.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.CustomerVerification.Services.VerificationSessionAppService
member.summary:
Tiger CS Ticketing's own business logic — not CRM business logic. Tiger CRM's entire role in verification is passive, read-only data access: given a unit number, it returns the unit's immutable CRM identifier and minimum display details, plus the contacts/owners/ tenants/authorized representatives linked to it (see ). Everything else — the and its state machine, selecting which returned contact is the requester, recording the verification method/result (channel-neutral — see 's remarks; this pilot's only caller uses a verbal read-back, ), deciding whether ticket creation may proceed, capturing the immutable verification-time snapshot, and the audit/authorization/ expiry rules around all of it — is owned here, by Tiger CS Ticketing. A future automated intake surface (e.g. Genesys AI voice/chat) that collects interaction data must call Tiger CS Ticketing's own API (this service, via POST /api/verification-sessions — a Ticketing endpoint) to have a requester verified; it must never implement these verification rules itself, and must never connect to a CRM system directly.
MVP-API-Contracts.md §2.4, simplified per MVP-Implementation-Backlog.md §0.2/S-07: unit/contact selection and verbal confirmation are combined into a single call against a single-use VerificationSessions row (MVP-ERD.md §2.24), rather than the full start/select/confirm/get four-endpoint flow. The confirmed session's snapshot fields are exactly what a later ticket-creation call (out of scope this phase, and itself also Ticketing's own business logic — see IntakeRecord in MVP-ERD.md §2.9, not yet built) would copy into TicketRequesterSnapshots (ADR-0007).
Idempotency — scope and upgrade path. plus a filtered unique index on (AgentEmployeeId, IdempotencyKey) (VerificationSessionConfiguration) is a pilot-scoped, module-local substitute for the approved generalized IdempotencyRecords mechanism (ADR-0014, MVP-Data-Dictionary.md §2.23), which has not been built yet (backlog S-05: "Audit trail, Outbox, and idempotency foundation"). It cannot conflict with that design: it lives entirely on VerificationSessions' own column/index, shares no table, no FK, and no Scope-string namespace with IdempotencyRecords or OutboxMessages. Its scope is exactly one thing — deduplicating 's create+confirm call on a double-submit or a genuine concurrent race (handled below via , not a plain check-then-insert, which would itself be a race). Upgrade path: when S-05 ships, this column and its check-then-insert/race-recovery logic should be replaced wholesale by a call through the generalized idempotency service against IdempotencyRecords (Scope = e.g. "CreateVerificationSession"), dropping the local column/index in the same migration — not layered alongside it.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.GenesysIntegration.Dto.GenesysCustomerLookupResultDto
member.summary:
What a Genesys call-pickup lookup answers.
Context, not a yes/no. The agent picking up needs to know who is calling and what they already have open, so this returns the customer, their units and their existing tickets — not a boolean.
Never a gate. being false is a perfectly normal answer, and it never stops the following Create Ticket call. Nor does a source being down: reports Failed alongside whatever the other sources did return.
member.param: The number that was searched — the caller's number after telephony normalization ("tel:+971…" is searched as "+971…"), or empty when the address carried no number at all (a withheld caller id).
True when at least one source matched a customer. False is a clean, expected answer.
The CRM Buyer Lookup outcome: Found, NotFound, AmbiguousMatch or Failed — or NotSearched when there was no number to search with.
The matched CRM Buyer (at most one) with every eligible unit, when CRM matched.
The PACT and Tasleeh results, each Found/NotFound/Failed with its matched customers and units.
The caller's existing tickets, newest first — open ones first within that. Empty when none are found or none are visible.
How many of the caller's tickets are still being worked.
The same answer flattened for a contact-center screen pop — see .

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.GenesysIntegration.Dto.GenesysScreenPopDto
member.summary:
The lookup reduced to flat, display-ready values — what a Genesys Data Action maps straight onto Architect variables and participant data, which cannot reliably pick a value out of the nested per-source arrays.
A projection, never a second answer. Every value is derived from the full result beside it, in a fixed order — CRM first (the verified Buyer record), then PACT, then Tasleeh — so the screen pop and the full result can never disagree. It never picks between two different customers: when the sources matched more than one, is the first in that order and says there were others, leaving identification to the agent exactly as the New Ticket wizard does.
Every string is empty rather than null when there is nothing to show, so a data action's output contract can declare them all as plain strings.
member.param: The matched customer's display name, or empty.
That customer's email, or empty.
Which source identified the customer: "Crm", "Pact" or "Tasleeh" — empty when none did.
The customer's id in that source, or empty.
How many customer records the sources matched in total. More than one means the agent must confirm who is calling.
Every unit found for the caller across all sources, as "Project - Unit" labels, de-duplicated.
The same labels joined with "; " — one string, for a display field that cannot show a list.
The caller's recent ticket numbers, in order.
The subset still being worked.
The recent tickets as one display string ("TG-… (InProgress); TG-… (Closed)").
Additive. The same de-duplicated units as , structured: display label plus the resolved PACT unit code. Expired PACT contracts are never listed. Same order and count as .

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.GenesysIntegration.Dto.GenesysHandoffRequestDto
member.summary:
Genesys reporting that an interaction needs a human agent — on any channel.
This is not a callback request. The same event covers a caller who reached an IVR, a website chat a bot could not finish, a WhatsApp thread that needs a person, and a social-media message a human must answer. What differs between them is , and even that is only recorded because the caller stated it — TigerCS never derives it from the channel.
member.param: The conversation needing a human. Its ticket and interaction already exist; this never creates either.

True when Genesys is handing straight over to a human (a live transfer), false when nobody is available and the work must wait. When true and an agent is named, the work item is recorded as Assigned rather than waiting.
"Callback", "ContinueChat", "ReplyInChannel" or "HumanTakeover" — omit when Genesys has not stated how the channel continues.
Why a human is needed (a virtual agent's escalation reason, a routing note). Free text: no vocabulary has been confirmed.

Why a human is needed, typed: "CustomerRequestedHuman", "AiConnectionLost", "AiEscalated", "RoutingDecision" or "AgentTransfer". Omit when Genesys does not state it — never derived from the end reason or the channel.
Genesys' own agent identifier, when one is already handling it.
The agent's display name, when supplied — recorded on the interaction.
Genesys' own routing-task/work-item identifier, if it supplies one. Used as the stronger idempotency key when present; never invented.
When Genesys decided a human was needed. Defaults to now when not supplied.
The ticket the human work belongs to, when the conversation carries several tickets. Absent resolves the conversation's default (first) ticket.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.GenesysIntegration.Dto.GenesysChannel
member.summary: The channel a Genesys inquiry arrived on, as TigerCS names it — the normalized boundary value, deliberately not Genesys' own media-type vocabulary (which is not confirmed). The integration/API edge maps whatever Genesys sends onto one of these; everything inside Ticketing speaks only this enum, and each value resolves to a configured Channel row for recording/reporting.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.GenesysIntegration.Dto.GenesysInquiryDto
member.summary:
The normalized Genesys inquiry — the only shape Ticketing's application layer understands, defined here on Ticketing's side of the boundary. Raw Genesys transport payloads never travel past TigerCS.Api's Genesys contracts: the API edge maps them onto this record, so no domain or application code depends on Genesys' JSON or its field names.
There is no event vocabulary. Receiving this inquiry means "create or reuse a ticket for this conversation" and nothing else. A ringing phone never reaches TigerCS at all — the phone flow starts when the agent picks up — so no Ringing/Answered/Started vocabulary is invented for Genesys to send.
Everything except and is optional, because Genesys' per-channel guarantees are not confirmed. Absent values are stored as null, never guessed. All four ticket-creating channels converge on this one contract and one ingestion flow — there is no per-channel ticket-creation path.
member.param: Required. Genesys' conversation identifier — the idempotency key and the permanent Ticket ↔ conversation link.
Required. Which TigerCS-normalized channel the inquiry arrived on.
Genesys' interaction id, where it differs from the conversation id and is supplied.
Genesys' customer-participant id, where supplied.
Genesys' communication id, where supplied.
"Inbound"/"Outbound" as reported, where available.
The customer's mobile number — the identity input the EXISTING TigerCS customer lookup searches with. Absent for a chat that collected no number.
The customer's name as the channel collected it (e.g. the website chat form's Full Name).
The customer's email as the channel collected it.
The Tiger number the customer dialed (Genesys-side datum; never used by Ticketing for routing).
The Genesys queue the inquiry was routed to — resolved to a department through the configured queue mapping when the customer selected no department.
The Genesys queue's display name, where supplied.
The Genesys agent handling the inquiry, where supplied.
The Genesys agent's display name, where supplied.
When the interaction started on the Genesys side (UTC), where supplied.
The department the customer explicitly selected — the website chat's Leasing / Customer Service / Maintenance choice. Takes priority over the queue mapping. Supply this OR , not both.
The same explicit selection expressed as a TigerCS department code, for a caller that knows codes rather than ids.
The tower/project the customer typed into the website chat form, where collected — carried onto the ticket as the manual project snapshot when no verified customer match exists.
The unit number the customer typed into the website chat form, where collected — see .
A short subject/summary the channel collected, where available. Used as the ticket's request summary; a generated, channel-named summary is used when absent.
The request type the bot identified, when it already has one; otherwise null and the ticket awaits classification in the human follow-up queue.

The caller's identifier of ONE distinct service request inside the conversation (e.g. "documents", "leasing"). A conversation may carry several; each (, ) pair is its own idempotent ticket. Absent keeps the original rule: the conversation is one ticket, and every repeat returns it.

true = this service request needs a person (leasing, a complaint). Such a ticket is never closed by the chatbot inactivity rules, by the AI or by document delivery — only by the authorized TigerCS workflow.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.GenesysIntegration.Dto.GenesysConversationEndDto
member.summary: The normalized end-of-conversation report, with the transcript available up to that moment. Sent when a conversation ends for ANY reason — the agent ended it, the customer closed the browser, the connection dropped, Genesys timed it out — so the interaction is always finalized and the conversation history is never lost.
member.param: Required. The conversation being ended — the same id the inquiry was ingested under.
When it ended (UTC). Defaults to the server's clock when Genesys supplies none.
Why it ended, as reported ("AgentDisconnect", "CustomerDisconnect", "Timeout", …). Free text until the contract fixes an enumeration.
The handling agent, where the end event names one and the interaction did not already know it.
The handling agent's display name — see .
The conversation's messages, in order. Empty/absent for a voice call, or for a chat that ended before anything was said.
The ticket whose interaction this ends, when the conversation carries several tickets; absent resolves the conversation's default (first) ticket.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.GenesysIntegration.Dto.GenesysInteractionContextDto
member.summary:
The integration boundary for Genesys-provided interaction context (Workflow/Automation phase 2). This DTO is the contract Ticketing needs — the fields Genesys is expected to hand over once an interaction is routed — deliberately defined here, on Ticketing's side of the boundary, because the exact Genesys API contracts are not finalized: nothing in this type assumes an endpoint shape, an auth model, or a payload encoding, and no Genesys API client exists in this phase.
Everything except the conversation id is optional, because Genesys' guarantees per channel are not confirmed — absent values are stored as null, never guessed. Interaction routing itself (Called Number → Queue, queue selection, agent selection) stays entirely inside Genesys; Ticketing persists this context verbatim for audit/traceability (TicketInteractionContext) and never re-derives routing from it.
Expected to be provided by Genesys later (per the operational design; to be confirmed with the finalized integration contract): channel, customer phone, called/destination number, queue id+name, agent id+name, conversation/interaction id, interaction start time, and direction where available. The customer phone still arrives through the existing intake (it is the verification identity input); when Genesys also supplies it, the intake value remains authoritative for verification. A future reverse direction (Ticketing → Genesys: ticket number/id, department, request type, status) is out of scope and only noted so this boundary stays extensible.
member.param: Required. Genesys' conversation/interaction id — the traceability link between a Ticket and the interaction.
The company/destination number the customer reached (Genesys-side datum; never used by Ticketing for routing).
The Genesys queue id the interaction was routed to, where provided.
The Genesys queue display name, where provided.
The Genesys agent id that handled the interaction, where provided.
The Genesys agent display name, where provided.
When the interaction started on the Genesys side (UTC), where provided.
Interaction direction as reported by Genesys (e.g. "Inbound"), where available.
The customer's name as the channel collected it (e.g. a website chat form's Full Name), where available — display/audit only, never a verified identity.
The customer's email as the channel collected it, where available — same display/audit-only status as .
The caller's identifier of the distinct service request this interaction (and ticket) is for, where the conversation carries several. Null for a conversation that is one ticket.
The ticket is human work from the start: no chatbot clock may close it.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.GenesysIntegration.Dto.GenesysTicketUpdateDto
member.summary:
Everything Genesys may update on a ticket it created — and, by omission, everything it may not.
This is deliberately a narrow surface. Genesys owns the conversation: who handled it, when it ended, what was said, and whether it still needs a human. It does not own the ticket's business state. There is no field here for category, request type, priority, status, owner, department, resolution or closure — those move only through their own TigerCS operations, with their own rules, authorization and SLA consequences. A field absent from this contract is a field Genesys cannot reach.
Every part is optional and independently idempotent: send only what changed, resend freely. In particular, ending a conversation that already ended does not move the recorded end time or duplicate its transcript, and no update here ever closes the ticket.
member.param: Required. The Genesys conversation this update belongs to. It must resolve to an interaction on the ticket in the route — that cross-check is what stops a transcript being applied to the wrong ticket.
The Genesys agent now handling the conversation, when known. Applied only if the interaction does not already name one.
That agent's display name, same apply-if-absent rule.
Set when the conversation has finished, for any reason — agent ended it, customer closed the browser, connection dropped, Genesys timed it out.
Set when the conversation needs a human agent, or when one has taken it. Omit entirely when neither applies.
When the interaction started on the Genesys side — recorded only if the creating call did not supply it; never moves once known.
Set when Genesys moved the conversation to another queue, or connected / transferred it to an agent. Omit when the routing did not change.
Set when the customer explicitly confirmed during the interaction that their issue is resolved. Record-only — never resolves or closes the ticket.
true starts the chatbot inactivity timer (a repeat never restarts it); false cancels it (the customer replied); null leaves it as it is.

true = the customer just did something in the conversation (sent a message, answered the bot): restarts the Website/Chatbot inactivity clock at TigerCS's own time. Send it on EVERY inbound customer message. null/false changes nothing.

true = the Genesys AI (voicebot / chatbot) finished the conversation: the ticket is closed (Resolved → Closed, reason "Closed by AI") — only if the AI still owns it. Refused, with a note and nothing changed, when a human is requested/pending/connected, a person owns the ticket, it is a Call Center ticket or it is already closed. null/false changes nothing.

Set when the bot has identified the request type: validated, then applied with its department routing, automatic assignment and SLA policy. Repeating the same one changes nothing; a different one replaces it only while no person has worked the ticket, otherwise it is refused.

true = this ticket needs a person: stops both chatbot inactivity clocks and forbids the AI and document delivery from closing it. Sticky — only the authorized TigerCS workflow ends it. null/false changes nothing.

Messages of the live conversation, sent as they happen or in batches. Additive and idempotent (de-duplicated on externalMessageId, else sender+time+body); does not end the conversation. The final ended.transcript may repeat them safely.
