member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.CustomerIdentityKind
member.summary: How a customer known to TigerCS is identified. TigerCS has no customer table: a customer is whatever the persisted tickets say about who raised them, so identity is resolved from the most stable fact each ticket carries, in this order — the CRM Buyer customer id, the persisted external-verification pair (source + external customer id), and only then the phone number captured by the intake the ticket was promoted from. A ticket with none of these has no customer identity and is not in the directory.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.CustomerHistoryDto
member.summary: Customer → Previous Ticket History. Sourced exclusively from the existing Tickets table — never a live CRM call — so this works even when CRM is offline. Exactly one identity is ever used per result: "Verified" means every ticket in shares the same CrmBuyerCustomerId (a phone number may match more than one CRM customer, so phone is never used to widen a verified customer's history); "Unverified" means there was no CrmBuyerCustomerId to key on and the persisted IntakeRecord.PhoneNumber snapshot was used as a fallback key instead — a weaker identity, and always labelled as such rather than silently presented the same way as CRM-verified history.
member.param: One of "Verified" (keyed by CrmBuyerCustomerId), "ExternalVerified" (keyed by the persisted external source + external customer id — PACT/Tasleeh), or "Unverified" (keyed by phone-number snapshot).
The CRM customer id this history was queried for, when is "Verified"; otherwise null.
The phone-number snapshot this history was queried for, when is "Unverified"; otherwise null.
Best-effort display name for the customer identity, when one is known (the CRM Buyer's ticket-time name snapshot). Null when no ticket in the history carried one.
Count of every matching ticket — not just the ones returned in .
Count of matching tickets whose TicketStatus is not Resolved or Closed.
Count of matching tickets whose TicketStatus is Resolved or Closed.
The newest tickets first, limited to the caller's requested page size — never the customer's entire history unbounded.
The external verification source this history was queried for, when is "ExternalVerified" (e.g. "Pact"/"Tasleeh"); otherwise null.
The source's own customer identifier this history was queried for, when is "ExternalVerified"; otherwise null.
The Customers directory key of this customer (crm:{id}, ext:{source}:{id} or phone:{number}) — the Customer Profile the Web links to; null when the anchor ticket has no customer identity.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.CustomerLookupUnitDto
member.summary: One unit associated with a matched customer, inside a . Business-rule change: a customer is never assumed to have exactly one unit — this is one entry in that customer's 0..N units. Only the fields the source's own gateway actually exposes are populated; a field the source doesn't have on file is left null rather than fabricated (e.g. only Crm ever populates the local reference ids, and Tasleeh exposes no unit data at all — see 's remarks).
member.param: The source's own immutable identifier for the unit — for Crm, its CrmUnitId.

The tower within the property, when the source has one on file.
The unit type, when the source has one on file.
This system's local cache id for the unit, when the source has one (Crm only) — pass this to ticket creation to link it.
This system's local cache id for the specific customer/unit relationship, when the source has one (Crm only) — pass this to ticket creation to link it.
The contract's end date, when the source has a readable one on file (PACT only); null otherwise.
True when falls before today's Dubai calendar date. Both lookup paths retain the contract for identity and historical reads; New Ticket excludes it from selectable units.
The PACT company associated with this contract, retained alongside the tenant for verified financial mapping.
PACT's own unit code for the contract, normalized (TP130-902-B), when PACT issued a listable one (PACT only); null otherwise. Used as unit identity — never derived from names.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.CustomerProfileDto
member.summary:
Customer Details/Profile — ticket-anchored, live CRM data for the Overview/Contact Info/Units tabs (Previous Tickets reuses CustomerHistoryDto unchanged, via the existing GET /api/tickets/{ticketId}/customer-history endpoint — this DTO carries none of that).
Identity is always the anchor ticket's own CrmBuyerCustomerId, never a live-refreshed value. is null only when the ticket itself was never CRM Buyer verified ( "NotCrmVerified") — there is no customer identity to show a profile for. Every other field comes from a fresh CrmBuyerLookupAppService.GetBuyerByPhoneAsync call (the same service the New Ticket wizard uses — never duplicated), so it reflects CRM's current data, not the ticket-time snapshot Ticket.CrmBuyerCustomerName/etc. already show elsewhere.
member.param: The anchor ticket's own CrmBuyerCustomerId, or null when the ticket was never CRM Buyer verified.

One of "NotCrmVerified", "Found", "CrmUnavailable", "AmbiguousCustomerMatch", "NotFoundInCrm", "NoPhoneOnRecord". Only "Found" populates the fields below. "NotFoundInCrm" also covers CRM resolving the ticket's phone to a different customer than — another customer's data is never shown just because the phone matches. "NoPhoneOnRecord" means the ticket has no intake phone to re-query CRM with (no linked IntakeRecord and no originating interaction).
The customer's name in English, when CRM records one.
The customer's name in Arabic, when CRM records one.
The customer's mobile number on file in CRM.
The customer's email, when CRM records one.
Every eligible (Sold/Contract, Buyer) unit this customer currently owns — not just the anchor ticket's own unit.

Composes the existing per-source DTO shapes rather than remapping them, so the workspace and the wizard can never drift apart on what a match looks like. Customer interactions waiting for a human to take them (AgentHandoffStatus.WaitingForAgent), in the departments the caller can see. Counts work items, not tickets: one ticket can carry several conversations over its life, and what this measures is people waiting to be spoken to.
How long the longest-waiting of those has waited, in seconds — the number that makes the queue's SLA risk legible. Zero when nothing is waiting.

The age at which a waiting interaction is rendered as at risk. Served with the data so the UI never hard-codes its own threshold, and configurable through Dashboard:HumanWaitRiskThresholdSeconds. Not an SLA. Human Wait is an operational KPI: it raises no breach row, no escalation and no SlaDeadlineType.
Distinct Closed tickets whose current cycle has a customer review submitted (Test-mode reviews excluded). Closed within the dashboard date range (latest closure date).
Distinct Closed tickets with no customer review for their current cycle. Same range (latest closure date).
Distinct Closed tickets whose latest closure was audited as AutoCloseByAi. Same range (latest closure date).
True while customer notifications run in test mode: Reviewed / Not Reviewed then evaluate Test-mode reviews (so UAT can validate them); production satisfaction statistics never include those.
Distinct Closed tickets whose latest closure was audited as Close (a person). Same range (latest closure date).

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.CreateIntakeRecordRequestDto
member.summary: The unconditional first step of intake (MVP-ERD.md §2.9) — created before customer lookup, for every interaction, unit-related or not, so none is ever silently lost.
member.param: Required. The selected channel from GET /api/channels — its numeric channelId (canonical), or its stable code (the seeded active codes are PHONE, WHATSAPP, LIVE_CHAT, SOCIAL_DM, WEBSITE, WALK_IN_KIOSK, MOBILE_APP, INSTAGRAM, FACEBOOK; codes match case-insensitively). The channel must exist and be active for a new ticket; it is configured under Admin → Configuration → Channels.

The identifier customer lookup searches CRM/PACT/Tasleeh with. Required when the selected channel's requiresPhone configuration is true (e.g. Phone), optional otherwise (e.g. Walk in / Kiosk). Preserved exactly as entered, regardless of what the lookup finds.

Optional. When given, customer lookup searches only the source(s) configured for this Department instead of CRM+PACT+Tasleeh. Never a promotion gate — a Department-scoped intake still promotes to a ticket exactly like any other.

Required. Whether the interaction is already known to concern a specific unit. The current New Ticket wizard always sends false here — the authoritative classification instead comes from a Unit selected via customer lookup after this call, which upgrades it automatically; this flag exists for a caller that already knows before lookup runs.

Optional, and independent of — never required for it, never required to be absent without it. The unit number exactly as the caller said it, before any lookup, kept only as an audit/intake note when it happens to be captured. Never the source of unit-related classification or ticket routing — the authoritative Unit is always the one resolved through customer lookup.
Optional. 1=Critical, 2=High, 3=Medium, 4=Low.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.ClassifyTicketRequestDto
member.summary: Classify an Unclassified ticket — the agent has read the inquiry and is recording what the customer actually wants.
member.param: Required. The real Ticket Category the agent selected. Must be active and must belong to the ticket's current department — a ticket is never filed under another department's category.
Required. The real priority. This is what selects the ticket's SLA policy, which is exactly why it is set here rather than guessed at creation.

Optional. The configured Request Type, when the agent can name it. Must be an active request type of the same department, and its workflow must have a Published version — the ticket is pinned to that version, exactly as it would have been had the request type been known at creation.
Required. The rowVersion from the ticket you read. A stale value is answered with 409.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketCreationOutcome.CrmBuyerAndManualProjectUnitBothSupplied
member.summary: A ticket may carry a real CRM Buyer match (CrmBuyerUnitId) or a manually-entered Project/Unit Number, never both.

member.summary: ExternalCustomerId/ExternalUnitId were supplied without a CustomerVerificationSource — external identifiers never travel without their source.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketCreationOutcome.CategoryNotFound
member.summary: CategoryId was supplied but does not resolve to an active Ticket Category.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketCreationOutcome.DepartmentOrCategoryRequired
member.summary: Neither a CategoryId nor a DepartmentId was supplied — a ticket needs one of the two to know where it belongs, and neither is ever invented.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketCreationOutcome.DepartmentNotFound
member.summary: DepartmentId was supplied for an unclassified ticket but does not resolve to an active Department.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketCreationOutcome.PriorityRequiresCategory
member.summary: A PriorityId was supplied without a CategoryId. An unclassified ticket carries no priority at all — priority is a judgement made at classification, alongside the category, never before it.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketCreationOutcome.DepartmentInactive
member.summary: Item 9 (senior review): the Category's routed Department is missing or deactivated — never silently route a ticket to a department nobody is staffing.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketCreationOutcome.CategoryDepartmentMismatch
member.summary: The IntakeRecord named a Department and the selected Category routes to a different one — the Category dropdown never offers this combination, so this only fires against a request built outside it.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketCreationOutcome.TicketNumberCollision
member.summary: A same-department, same-day TicketNumber collision (real DB unique-index race) — nothing else was touched; retrying the whole request is always correct.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketCreationOutcome.RequestTypeWorkflowNotPublished
member.summary: The selected request type's workflow has no Published version to pin the ticket to — an administration gap (the workflow is still a Draft), never silently ignored.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketCreationOutcome.RequestTypeNotFound

member.summary: One interaction of a ticket's conversation history — the call or chat itself plus, for text channels, its full transcript. Ordered chronologically alongside the ticket's other interactions.
member.param: The interaction.
True on the one interaction the ticket was created from.
"Genesys" or "Ticketing" — who produced the interaction context.
The channel the interaction happened on.
That channel's display name, resolved from channel configuration — still shown for a channel that has since been deactivated.
The customer's phone number for this interaction, as captured.
The customer's name as the channel reported it, where available.
The customer's email as the channel reported it, where available.
"Inbound"/"Outbound" as reported, where available.
The Genesys conversation this interaction records, or null for a locally-created (walk-in) interaction.
The Genesys queue the inquiry was routed to, where reported.
That queue's display name, where reported.
The handling agent's display name, where reported.
The handling agent's Genesys identifier, where reported.
When the interaction started on the Genesys side, where reported; otherwise when Ticketing recorded it.
When the conversation ended/disconnected, or null while it is still live (or was never reported ended).
Why it ended, as reported.
"Ended" once an end was recorded, otherwise "Active" — the INTERACTION's own lifecycle, which is independent of the ticket's status.
The transcript, in order. Empty for a voice call, and for a chat with nothing recorded.

The pending human work raised from this interaction, when there is any — so an agent opening the ticket sees why a human was asked for and where that work stands, beside the transcript that led to it. Null when this interaction never needed a human.

Who is handling a Genesys interaction right now: "Ai" (the virtual agent is the only participant), "WaitingForHuman" (a human was explicitly requested and nobody has taken it) or "Human" (a person took it, spoke, or — on the phone — answered). Null for an interaction Ticketing created itself. Independent of the ticket's status and of whether the interaction has ended.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketListRequestDto
member.summary: Filtering, sorting, and paging for the ticket queue (MVP-API-Contracts.md §3.2). Bound from the query string; every filter is optional and combines with AND.
member.param: Narrow to one department. Cannot widen what the caller may already see.
Narrow to one category.
Narrow to one priority. 1=Critical, 2=High, 3=Medium, 4=Low.
Narrow to one status: Open, InProgress, PendingCustomer, Resolved, Closed. The retired PendingThirdParty is no longer an offered filter.
Narrow to one verification status: Unverified, PendingCrmVerification, Verified.
Narrow to tickets currently owned by one employee.
Free-text search over the ticket number and request summary.
Which field to sort by.
Sort direction — asc or desc.
1-based page number.
Page size.
Narrow to tickets whose originating interaction arrived on one channel (Dashboard drill-down).
Narrow to one request type (Dashboard drill-down).

True: only active tickets — Open, InProgress, PendingCustomer, and any historical ticket still in the legacy PendingThirdParty (the Dashboard's Open Tickets). A legacy pending ticket is non-terminal work and stays in the active set, so it never disappears from a queue before someone returns it to InProgress.
True: only active tickets with no current owner — sitting in their department's queue.
True: only active tickets whose SLA state is Breached.
True: only active tickets whose current, unbreached SLA resolution deadline falls today (UTC calendar day).
Narrow active tickets to one age bucket by CreatedAtUtc: Under24Hours, OneToThreeDays, ThreeToSevenDays, OverSevenDays.
True: only tickets carrying a Pending approval the caller is authorized to action.
Only tickets created on or after this UTC calendar day.
Only tickets created on or before this UTC calendar day.

True: only tickets with no request type (nobody — human or Genesys AI — has classified them yet). A filter on the ticket queue only: it never implies, requests or creates a human handoff, and department visibility applies exactly as for every other filter.

Only Closed tickets in one Dashboard closure KPI: Reviewed (customer feedback submitted), NotReviewed, ClosedByAi (latest closure audited as AutoCloseByAi) or ClosedByAgent (latest closure audited as Close).
Only Closed tickets whose latest closure was on or after this UTC calendar day (Dashboard closure KPIs).
Only Closed tickets whose latest closure was on or before this UTC calendar day.

True ("Created by Me"): only tickets the caller created — including ones that have since moved to another department, which a CS Agent keeps read-only access to. Never widens visibility: it only narrows the caller's own scope.

Supervisor review: only tickets an agent passed up as UnableToResolve or NeedsEscalation. Requires a supervisory role (CS Supervisor, CS Manager, Department Head, General Manager, Chairman/CEO); other callers get 403. Narrows the caller's normal visibility, never widens it.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketListRequestDto.CreatedFrom
member.summary: Only tickets created on or after this UTC calendar day.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketListRequestDto.CreatedTo
member.summary: Only tickets created on or before this UTC calendar day.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketListRequestDto.Unclassified
member.summary: True: only tickets with no request type (nobody — human or Genesys AI — has classified them yet). A filter on the ticket queue only: it never implies, requests or creates a human handoff, and department visibility applies exactly as for every other filter.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketListRequestDto.ClosureCategory
member.summary: Only Closed tickets in one Dashboard closure KPI: Reviewed (customer feedback submitted), NotReviewed, ClosedByAi (latest closure audited as AutoCloseByAi) or ClosedByAgent (latest closure audited as Close).

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketListRequestDto.ClosedFrom
member.summary: Only Closed tickets whose latest closure was on or after this UTC calendar day (Dashboard closure KPIs).

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketListRequestDto.ClosedTo
member.summary: Only Closed tickets whose latest closure was on or before this UTC calendar day.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketListRequestDto.CreatedByMe
member.summary: True ("Created by Me"): only tickets the caller created — including ones that have since moved to another department, which a CS Agent keeps read-only access to. Never widens visibility: it only narrows the caller's own scope.

member.name: P:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketListRequestDto.Escalated
member.summary: Supervisor review: only tickets an agent passed up as UnableToResolve or NeedsEscalation. Requires a supervisory role (CS Supervisor, CS Manager, Department Head, General Manager, Chairman/CEO); other callers get 403. Narrows the caller's normal visibility, never widens it.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.TicketDetailDto
member.summary: Full ticket detail (MVP-API-Contracts.md §3.3), and the response of every ticket write.
member.param: The ticket.
The human-facing ticket number.
The department the ticket was raised in.
The department that currently holds it.
The current owner, or null when unassigned — including immediately after a transfer.
The verified unit, or null while the ticket is provisional.
The verified contact, or null while the ticket is provisional.
The ticket's category, or null while the ticket is Unclassified — no category is ever invented to fill it.
1=Critical, 2=High, 3=Medium, 4=Low, or null while Unclassified: no priority has been judged, so none is shown and none selects an SLA policy.
One of Open, InProgress, PendingCustomer, Resolved, Closed — or the legacy, no-longer-reachable PendingThirdParty on a historical ticket.
One of Unverified, PendingCrmVerification, Verified.
One of None, Level1, Level2, Level3, Level4.
One of Running, Paused, Met, Breached, NotApplicable.
Set once the ticket is resolved. 1=Resolved, 2=Cancelled, 3=Rejected, 4=Duplicate.
The ticket this one duplicates, when the outcome is Duplicate.
The request, in the agent's words.
How many times the ticket has been reopened.
When the ticket was created, in UTC.
The concurrency token, Base64-encoded. Send it back on the next write to this ticket.
The real CRM Buyer Lookup match's customer id, or null when no CRM Buyer match was linked at creation.
The matched CRM Lead id, or null.
The matched CRM unit id, or null.
The matched CRM project id, or null.
Ticket-time display snapshot of the matched Buyer's name, or null.
Ticket-time display snapshot of the matched unit's project name, or null.
Ticket-time display snapshot of the matched unit's number, or null.
The agent-entered Project name, when no CRM Buyer match was linked at creation.
The agent-entered Unit Number, when no CRM Buyer match was linked at creation.
The external lookup source that verified the customer at creation ("Pact"/"Tasleeh"), or null for CRM Buyer tickets and plain manual entry.
The source's own customer identifier (for PACT, its tenantID) — an external identifier only, never a local reference.
The source's own identifier for the selected unit (for PACT, its unitID) — an external identifier only.

When the current resolution was recorded, in UTC — null while the ticket has no current resolution. Populated on detail reads (GET /api/tickets/{id}); write responses leave it null and clients re-read.
The configured request type the ticket follows, or null for a ticket created without one.
The request type's name — populated on detail reads.
The exact workflow VERSION the ticket was pinned to at creation; null for a ticket with no request type. Never changes after creation.
The pinned version's workflow name — populated on detail reads.
The pinned version's number ("V2") — populated on detail reads.

The channel the ticket ENTERED the system on (its originating interaction's channel) — never changed by later interactions on other channels; null for tickets predating the interaction model. Populated on detail reads.
The originating channel's display name, resolved from channel configuration — still shown for a channel that has since been deactivated. Populated on detail reads.

True when the caller may open this ticket but change nothing on it: they created it, it is outside their department, and they hold no other grant on it. The server refuses every modification (403) regardless; the UI uses this to hide the actions. Populated on detail reads.
The employee who created the ticket. Populated on detail reads.
False while the ticket has no Category yet — an inquiry captured before anyone read the request. The UI shows "Unclassified" and offers the classify action rather than rendering a missing category.

The first mapped Genesys agent who handled the originating interaction; null for non-Genesys tickets and when no agent was recorded. Never changes after it is set, and is separate from CurrentOwnerEmployeeId.
Who recorded the current resolution; null until resolved (and for system closures this is the system actor on the resolution row).
How many times the ticket changed hands by a person's action (department transfers and reassignments). Automatic request-type routing is not counted.
How many of those were recorded as UnableToResolve or NeedsEscalation.
Display name of FirstHandledByEmployeeId, read from the employee directory itself — so it resolves even when that person has since left the department or been deactivated.
Display name of ResolvedByEmployeeId, resolved the same way.

Whether this ticket is waiting on a human agent, derived from the one open TicketAgentHandoff row: WaitingForAgent, Assigned or InProgress while work is outstanding, and "NotRequired" when none is. Deliberately not a column on the ticket — a ticket accumulates many interactions, and a persisted copy would be a second source of truth free to drift from the row that actually owns this state.
When the outstanding human work was raised — the start of the Human Wait metric. Null when nothing is outstanding.

Whether FR-RES-04's lifecycle rule currently allows Reopen — Closed, closed as Resolved, and within the ISSUE-011 window measured from closure. Lifecycle only, never a permission statement: the Reopen endpoint separately enforces TicketRoleSets.Reopen AND the caller's access to the ticket. Populated on detail reads; false on write responses.
When the ticket reached Closed, in UTC, read from lifecycle history — the moment the reopen window is measured from. Null while the ticket is not closed. Populated on detail reads.

member.summary: Assign or reassign a ticket (MVP-API-Contracts.md §3.5).

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.AgentHandoffAppService
member.summary:
The agent-facing half of pending human work: seeing what is waiting, and taking it, finishing it, or standing it down.
Deliberately not a routing engine. Nothing here decides who should get the work, dials anyone, sends a WhatsApp message or resumes a chat. Genesys owns channel delivery, queue routing, agent availability, live transfer and outbound execution. This service owns the business-visible state of the work: who is waiting, since when, on which channel, for which ticket, and whether a human has picked it up.
Nothing here touches the ticket. Completing human work is not resolving a case: the customer whose chat was answered may still have an NOC workflow running for days. The ticket keeps following the existing TigerCS lifecycle, and the two statuses are read side by side.
Every mutation is idempotent. Starting work already in progress, or completing work already completed, is answered rather than duplicated — a double-clicked button and a redelivered event behave the same way.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.AgentHandoffAppService.AcceptAsync(System.Guid,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{System.String},System.Int64,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
A human agent accepts pending work: claims it exclusively, takes ownership of the ticket behind it, and starts the work — all in one transaction, or none of it.
Exclusive. refuses a second agent with the holder's identity, so the loser is told who has it instead of receiving a success carrying someone else's name. The same agent repeating the call is idempotent. The handoff's RowVersion closes the narrower window where two requests both read an unclaimed row and interleave their commits.
Department membership is a PRECONDITION, not a conditional. An employee may accept only if they are an active member of the ticket's CurrentDepartmentId. Checked before a single thing is written, so a caller who cannot own the ticket changes nothing at all: the handoff stays , its AssignedEmployeeId stays null, and the ticket stays Open and unowned. They receive .
Why a precondition rather than "assign where possible". Accepting is one indivisible business act — take the work, own the ticket, start it. Claiming the work while declining to assign the ticket produces the state this method exists to avoid: handoff InProgress, which tells the queue somebody is on it, while the ticket sits Open and unowned, which tells the ticket nobody is. The invariant being protected is MVP-API-Contracts.md §3.5's — an assignee must belong to the ticket's current department, which TicketAssignmentAppService.AssignAsync already refuses as EmployeeNotInDepartment — and it is not relaxed here.
The cross-department route is Department Transfer. A human from another department who needs this work transfers the ticket first (POST /api/tickets/{id}/transfer); a member of the new current department then accepts. The handoff's own department follows the ticket, so the work stays on the same list it always was.
ADR-0024's override does not reach the membership rule. It still carries authorization and visibility — a System Administrator sees and may act on this work in any department — but membership of the assignee is a domain invariant about the ticket's data, not a permission, so the administrator is refused here exactly as anyone else is. That is why the check below calls the repository directly rather than through AuthorizationGate.
First Response is deliberately NOT recorded here (confirmed decision 10). Accepting is not replying: the customer has heard nothing yet. Ticket.FirstHumanResponseAtUtc is satisfied by the first actual human message — see GenesysConversationEndAppService's transcript path. Acceptance time is the end of the separate Human Wait operational metric (RequestedAtUtc → AssignedAtUtc), which is not an SLA.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.CustomerHistoryAppService
member.summary:
Customer → Previous Ticket History. Reads exclusively from the existing Tickets (and, for the unverified fallback, IntakeRecords) tables — never a live CRM call — so history is available even when CRM is offline.
Three identities, never combined. A CRM-verified customer's identity is Ticket.CrmBuyerCustomerId — a phone number may match more than one CRM customer, so history for a verified customer is always scoped by the exact selected CrmBuyerCustomerId, never widened by phone. An externally-verified customer's identity (PACT/Tasleeh) is the persisted Ticket.CustomerVerificationSource + Ticket.ExternalCustomerId pair — never a display-name or phone match, so two different customers sharing similar contact data can never share a history. Only when a ticket carries neither identity does this service fall back to the persisted IntakeRecord.PhoneNumber snapshot linked to that ticket — a weaker identity (one phone number can belong to more than one real customer), so that result is always labelled "Unverified" rather than presented the same way as verified history.
Authorization: identical department visibility to the ticket queue/detail (TicketQueryAppService), never widened. Knowing a CRM customer id, an external customer id, or a ticket id never grants access to a ticket the caller could not otherwise see — every query here is scoped by the caller's own visible departments, and the ticket-anchored lookup additionally checks the anchor ticket's own department visibility before running anything.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.CustomerLookupAppService
member.summary:
Business-rule change: searches CRM, PACT, and/or Tasleeh by the intake's phone number and returns whatever each searched source found — this is enrichment/identification for the agent, never a Ticket creation gate (see TicketCreationAppService.CreateAsync, which accepts an optional matched unit/contact pair but never requires one).
Which sources are searched depends on the intake's Department, not a hard-coded rule. An IntakeRecord with no DepartmentId searches all three sources. One with a DepartmentId searches only the source(s) configured for that Department ( — data-driven, not an if (departmentId == ...) branch per department) — including zero sources if none are configured, never silently falling back to "search everything".
Sources are searched independently, in parallel, and never let one another's failure hide a result. Each of / / catches only its own source's unavailable exception; a source that cannot be reached comes back Failed, a source that answers with nothing comes back NotFound, and both are returned alongside whatever the other searched source(s) found (e.g. CRM: Found, PACT: Failed, Tasleeh: NotFound all in the same response) — this call itself never throws for any of that, and never rejects the request. A source that was never searched (out of Department scope) has no entry at all — never a fake NotFound standing in for "not queried".
CRM matches reuse the existing cache-aside upsert. A CRM phone match is resolved to this system's own local UnitReferenceId/ ContactReferenceId via — the same tested upsert path CrmController's unit-number lookups already use — so a match found here can be passed straight to ticket creation. PACT and Tasleeh have no equivalent local reference table: a match from either is pure display enrichment, never linked to a Ticket by id (see 's remarks).
PACT contracts remain available for identity, history and Collections. Both lookup paths retain expired contracts, flagged with . The New Ticket unit-selection view excludes expired contracts. Filtering the source result here would discard evidence linking CRM to a historical PACT tenant, and hide the tenant's historical tickets and financial mapping.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.CustomerLookupAppService.SearchExternalSourcesByPhoneAsync(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Customer Workspace search (no IntakeRecord yet): the same PACT and Tasleeh legs the intake-anchored runs, exposed for a raw phone number so the Dashboard's customer search can reuse them without creating an intake record first. CRM is deliberately not part of this method — the workspace's CRM identity comes from the real CRM Buyer Lookup (CrmBuyerLookupAppService), exactly as the New Ticket wizard already does; running the fixture-backed generic CRM leg here would only duplicate it. All department-source configuration stays intake-scoped: a pre-intake search has no department, so both external sources are always asked. Expired PACT contracts are returned here, flagged — the workspace must still find a customer whose contracts have all ended (see this type's remarks).

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.CustomerLookupAppService.SearchCrmAsync(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Business-rule change: a phone number may match several distinct Buyers, and each Buyer may own several units — never assumed to be one of either. Every matched Buyer's every unit is resolved to this system's own local UnitReference/ContactReference cache ids via the same tested cache-aside upsert already used (), one unit at a time, so each unit in the response carries the correct pair to pass straight to ticket creation for that specific customer/unit relationship.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.CustomerLookupAppService.SearchPactAsync(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
PACT's outcome-wrapped port never throws (see 's remarks): NotFound maps to a NotFound source entry, and every other non-Success outcome (Unavailable, Unauthorized, InvalidResponse) collapses to Failed — the same "reported, never blocking" treatment the throwing sources get from their catch blocks. PACT contracts/units carry no local UnitReferenceId/ContactReferenceId (no cache table exists for PACT), so every unit is display enrichment for the agent — all current units are returned and none is ever auto-selected.
All contracts, including expired ones, remain available as identity evidence and for historical reads. Selectability belongs to New Ticket.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.CustomerProfileAppService
member.summary:
Customer Details/Profile — the Overview/Contact Info/Units tabs on the Customer Profile page. Ticket-anchored, exactly like : the identity (CrmBuyerCustomerId) and the department-visibility check both come from the anchor ticket, never from a caller-supplied phone number or CRM id — a caller cannot use this to browse a customer they could not otherwise see via Ticket Details.
Thin orchestration only — no CRM logic duplicated. This service does exactly four things: authorize against the ticket (reusing , same as Ticket Details itself), resolve the phone number the ticket was verified against (see below), delegate the actual CRM search to — the same service the New Ticket wizard's CRM Buyer Lookup step uses, through the same real ICrmBuyerLookupGateway — and confirm the Buyer CRM returned is the ticket's own persisted customer. It re-filters nothing, selects no unit, and re-queries CRM through nothing else: the older generic ICrmGateway port (unit-number lookup, Mock-only at this phase) is deliberately not a dependency here — every field the profile shows is already carried by .
Phone resolution. CRM is searched by phone number only, and the phone is never caller-supplied: it comes from the IntakeRecord this ticket was promoted from (the same resolution uses for its unverified fallback), or — for a ticket with no linked IntakeRecord — from the ticket's originating TicketInteraction, which persists the same intake phone at creation time. A CRM-verified ticket with neither on record reports "NoPhoneOnRecord" rather than pretending CRM was asked and could not answer.
Identity is validated, never inferred from the phone alone. A phone number can be reassigned in CRM after the ticket was created. The Buyer CRM returns is accepted only when its CustomerId equals the ticket's persisted CrmBuyerCustomerId; any other customer is reported as "NotFoundInCrm" (CRM no longer resolves this phone to this customer) and logged for investigation, so the page never silently shows a different customer's name, contact details or units.
Live CRM data, unlike Customer History. Previous Tickets on the Customer Profile page reuses CustomerHistoryAppService unchanged (via its own existing endpoint) precisely because history must work with CRM offline; Overview/Contact Info/Units cannot make that promise — full name (Arabic), mobile number, email, and the customer's full current unit list simply do not exist anywhere in Ticketing's own persisted data, only in CRM. When CRM cannot be searched (unavailable, no longer finds a match, or a data-integrity conflict), says so and the caller still knows the ticket's own CrmBuyerCustomerId.

Whether the selected channel's RequiresPhone setting is enforced. True — the default, and what every agent-driven caller uses — is the Create Ticket Step 1 rule: the wizard must not let an agent proceed without a number the channel needs.
False is for an automated intake, and exists so an inquiry is never discarded. A Genesys inquiry records whatever the channel actually supplied: a caller who withheld their number, or a social-media direct message that carries none, has no phone to capture, and refusing the intake would throw away a real customer interaction — the exact outcome exists to prevent ("no interaction is ever silently lost"). The setting still governs every agent-facing path unchanged; nothing about the stored record differs, and a phone that IS supplied is stored and searched exactly as always.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.ReopenActivityFacts
member.summary:
The machine-readable facts of one reopen, as carried on the TicketWorkflowEvent.Reopened row's Note — the department it moved between, what happened to ownership, the new Resolution SLA deadline, and which reopen cycle this was.
Why here and not in new columns. Ticket Details has to be able to render "Department: Customer Service → Handover · Resolution SLA due: …" beside the reason, and the approved rule asks for that to reuse the existing lifecycle stores rather than a new activity table. The typed event row already exists, is already append-only, and is already served by GET /api/tickets/{ticketId}/approvals; its Note is documented as short display context. So the facts ride there, and — because the entity rightly says consumers must never key on free text — writer and reader share this one formatter/parser instead of each inventing a string format.
Bounded by construction. Only identifiers, a flag and one round-tripped timestamp are written — never the caller's reason, which lives in the TicketStatusHistory row where free text belongs. That keeps the note comfortably inside the column's 500-character limit whatever the agent typed.
member.param: The department the ticket was closed in.
The department that took the reopened work on. May equal .
Who owned it at closure; null if it was already unassigned.
Who the assignment automation landed on; null means the department queue.
The new Resolution cycle's deadline; null when the ticket has no SLA clock.
Which reopen this was — 1 for the first.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.ReopenPolicy
member.summary:
ISSUE-011's approved decision (Executive-Decisions.md row 17): a ticket may be reopened within a fixed window — 7 days by default, configurable (Ticketing:ReopenWindowDays, bound at DI registration), never hard-coded at call sites. Beyond the window a new linked ticket is created instead (BR-020) — the window check therefore yields a distinct outcome, never a generic "not eligible".
The window is measured from closure, not from resolution. Under the approved Closed-only rule the reopenable event is the close, so the clock starts at the moment the ticket reached . A Closed ticket carries no closure timestamp of its own, so callers read it from the lifecycle history that Close already writes — the TicketStatusHistory row for the transition into Closed (ITicketStatusHistoryRepository.GetLatestTransitionIntoAsync) — rather than substituting the resolution timestamp, which for a ticket resolved long before it was closed would silently shorten the window.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketApprovalAppService
member.summary:
Approvals and dependency events (Workflow/Automation phase 3): request / approve / reject / cancel an approval cycle, and record the typed prerequisite/maintenance events — all configuration-driven (the ticket's request type must configure the approval), all audited, and all independent of TicketStatus. The approval record is the authoritative approval state; a ticket that also waits operationally uses the existing structured Pending Internal, as a separate concern.
No SLA is calculated here. An approval decision only produces its typed (ApprovalReceived / CustomerServiceApproved / ApprovalRejected) with a trustworthy timestamp; phase 4 reads those events as its conditional trigger source.
No automatic resume. When an approval is granted, the ticket's Pending state (if any) stays until an authorized user explicitly resumes via the existing status change — whether approval auto-resumes the ticket is an open business decision (docs/Workflow-Approvals-Phase3.md).
Provisional approver authorization (fail-safe, documented): the decision is gated by the approval's target snapshot — a role target needs that role; an employee target needs that exact employee; a department target needs active membership of that department AND one of (or the requirement's narrowing role). Nothing broader is granted; the exact Accounting and CS approver roles remain open business decisions, and the ADR-0024 System Administrator override applies through exactly as it does for every other permission rule.
is a request, not a reopen. It is the one type requestable on a Closed ticket — every other type stays refused there — and it exists so that a role without direct Reopen can ask for one. Granting it writes the decision, the typed event and the audit row and touches nothing on the ticket: no status change, no department move, no owner change, no SLA cycle, no customer email. The reopen itself remains TicketLifecycleAppService.ReopenAsync, performed afterwards by a CS user who supplies a target department and a current RowVersion, and which revalidates every rule at that moment. An approved cycle is therefore never a bypass and never a precondition — direct Reopen is unchanged and needs no approval.

It only ever fills a gap. It does nothing when the ticket already has an owner, when the configured request-type rule made a decision (, or an explicit ), when the department's workflow settings disable assignment, or when the creator is not an active member of the ticket's current department (the same invariant every assignment honours). member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketClassificationAppService
member.summary:
The Unclassified → Classified transition: an agent has read the inquiry and records what the customer actually wants.
The same ticket is classified in place. No second ticket is created, nothing is copied, and the ticket keeps its number, its department, its interactions and its whole history — a customer who started one conversation has one ticket, before and after.
The SLA clock is never restarted here. A Genesys ticket is created on the default (Normal) priority with its SLA period already running from creation, so classifying it adds the category (and request type) to the running period: a more urgent priority tightens it under the earlier-of rule, a less urgent one needs the approved-downgrade flow. Only a ticket that has no priority and no period (created before default priorities existed, or while none was configured) starts its clock here — from now, the classification timestamp, never backdated, since no target existed before.
First Response is measured separately and is unaffected. Ticket.FirstHumanResponseAtUtc lives on the ticket, not on the SLA period, so an agent's first reply to an unclassified Genesys inquiry is recorded with its real timestamp exactly as on any other ticket — how quickly the customer reached a human stays measurable from the moment the inquiry arrived, whether or not anyone has classified it yet.
A ticket that was created classified is untouched by all of this: it already has its category, its priority and its SLA period, and this service performs initial classification only (). That refusal is a Phase 1 safeguard while reclassification semantics are undefined — see — not a rule that a classification may never change.

Ticket.FirstHumanResponseAtUtc lives on the ticket, not on the SLA period, so an agent's first reply to an unclassified Genesys inquiry is recorded with its real timestamp exactly as on any other ticket — how quickly the customer reached a human stays measurable from the moment the inquiry arrived, whether or not anyone has classified it yet.
A ticket that was created classified is untouched by all of this: it already has its category, its priority and its SLA period, and this service performs initial classification only (). That refusal is a Phase 1 safeguard while reclassification semantics are undefined — see — not a rule that a classification may never change.

member.summary:
Business-rule change: a single ticket-creation path for every IntakeRecord — unit-related or not. Customer information from CRM, PACT, or Tasleeh is attached when the agent already resolved a match via (/ ); lack of a match never prevents ticket creation. The only thing every ticket requires is a valid, active Ticket Category. This method inspects the request and the IntakeRecord itself and creates the appropriate internally — when a resolved unit/contact pair is supplied, otherwise — rather than exposing a separate endpoint per case.
Two SaveChanges calls, in one real transaction. Both and use database-generated identity PKs (bigint), so a 's real TicketId is not known until its own insert commits — but linking the IntakeRecord and writing the requester snapshot/status-history/audit rows all need that real ID. The ticket is therefore inserted alone first; everything else commits in a second call — both wrapped in one scope. A TicketNumber unique-index collision on the first call () is translated to — a clean, retryable 409 rather than an unhandled exception; nothing has been touched yet at that point, so retrying the whole request is always correct.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketCreationAppService.EnqueueTicketCreatedAsync(TigerCS.Domain.Modules.Ticketing.Ticket,System.Guid,System.Guid,System.DateTime,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Writes MVP-API-Contracts.md §3.1's TicketCreated Outbox event — the one that "drives the automated acknowledgement notification" (FR-NOT-01) — into the same transaction as the ticket itself.
Nothing is sent from here. NFR-REL-01 is explicit that nothing is dispatched from application code inside a request handler without first being durably recorded in the same transaction as the state change. This method records; ADR-0015's recurring dispatcher delivers, after the commit. A caller that rolls back — a ticket-number collision — takes this row down with it, so a ticket that does not exist can never acknowledge anything.
Written for an unverified ticket too, deliberately. FR-NOT-01's acceptance criterion is "email attempted for every ticket", and an unverified ticket has no requester snapshot to resolve a recipient from. Skipping the event would make that ticket invisible — indistinguishable from one that was acknowledged — whereas enqueuing it produces a dead-lettered, audited, countable record that no acknowledgement could be sent and why.
A null return means the key was already reserved — the same logical event is already enqueued, so no second message is written. That is the normal outcome of a retried request, not an error, and no audit entry is written for it because nothing was queued.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketLifecycleAppService.ReopenAsync(System.Guid,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{System.String},System.Int64,TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Dto.ReopenTicketRequestDto,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Reopen (MVP-API-Contracts.md §3.11, FR-RES-04), implementing the approved business rule. A Closed ticket — and only a Closed one, closed as Resolved — returns to InProgress in a department the reopening CS user names, unowned, with a fresh Resolution SLA cycle.
Authorization is two-part. The role gate is the CS layer — CS Agent, CS Supervisor and CS Manager (), the final approved rule — and it is followed by a resource-level check that the caller could see this ticket at all (), so enumerating ticket ids reaches nothing the agent was not already entitled to. Both run through , so ADR-0024's System Administrator override applies as it does to every other operation.
Concurrency is checked before eligibility, deliberately inverting the order this method used to run in. Two agents reopening at once both hold the pre-reopen RowVersion; the loser used to find the ticket already InProgress and be told "not eligible for reopen", which is true but misleading — nothing is wrong with the ticket, their copy is stale. Comparing the token first answers that race with the concurrency conflict it actually is, and the optimistic check at SaveChanges still covers the narrower window between this read and the commit. Either way the second request writes nothing: no second cycle, no second event, no second email.
Everything commits together — the domain transition, the archived resolution, the new SLA cycle, the re-run of the existing assignment automation, the lifecycle history, the typed Reopened event Ticket Details renders, the audit entries and the customer-email Outbox row — under one correlation id, or nothing does.

Classifies a request type onto an existing ticket and applies everything the request type configures, in the caller's transaction: its workflow version (pinned), its responsible department (through the same transfer semantics as TicketAssignmentAppService.TransferAsync), the configured automatic assignment, and its SLA policy.
Used for Genesys tickets, which are created before the request type is known. The ticket is created in the department the interaction arrived in; OriginatingDepartmentId is therefore never rewritten — only CurrentDepartmentId moves, via (which also clears the owner, so the receiving department's rule or queue decides). The routing is a system action driven by configuration, so it is not gated on the CS-Manager-only manual transfer role and does not consult the source department's "allow transfers out" setting; the configured request-type department is the authority.
Assignment stays automatic and fail-safe. picks the configured assignee; no rule, a stale assignee or a department that disables assignment leave the ticket in the responsible department's queue. A ticket that already has an owner and does not move departments keeps its owner.
The SLA is adjusted, never restarted. See . Routing and assignment never touch FirstHumanResponseAtUtc.

Assignment stays automatic and fail-safe. picks the configured assignee; no rule, a stale assignee or a department that disables assignment leave the ticket in the responsible department's queue. A ticket that already has an owner and does not move departments keeps its owner.
The SLA is adjusted, never restarted. See . Routing and assignment never touch FirstHumanResponseAtUtc.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketRoleSets
member.summary:
Per-action role sets for ticket-operations authorization (Solution-Analysis.md §4.1's permission matrix, ISSUE-022's approved Resolve/Close split, Security-Architecture.md §3's CS-layer cross-department scoping). Each action gets its own set rather than reusing one blanket list — DepartmentScopedRequirement was already built constructor-parameterized for exactly this reason, per its own remarks ("flagged for confirmation before a real ticket endpoint consumes this policy") — this is that endpoint, and this is the resolution.
System Administrator is deliberately absent from the operational sets below, and is authorized anyway. Every consumer of this class routes its decision through AuthorizationGate, which applies the AuthorizationOverride (ADR-0024 — confirmed management decision) before the set is consulted. Adding the role to these lists instead would be the per-call-site duplication that correction's requirement 4 explicitly rules out, and would lose the distinction these sets exist to record: what each role is granted by the permission matrix, as against what the override grants on top of it.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketRoleSets.CrossDepartmentView
member.summary: View (queue/detail): cross-department for CS-layer roles (Security-Architecture.md §3, already the exact role list PolicyNames.DepartmentScoped was defined with) plus GM/Chairman/ SysAdmin, who hold "View: All tickets"/"All (technical)" in Solution-Analysis.md §4.1. Department Employee/Head are scoped to their own department membership(s), not included here.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketRoleSets.CrossDepartmentSupervisory
member.summary: Status change ("work" sub-machine — Open→InProgress, InProgress↔Pending*): cross-department authority for Supervisor+, on top of the ticket's current owner (checked separately in TicketLifecycleAppService). Chairman/CEO is deliberately absent: the role is read-only by agreed management decision (audit F-5) and holds no status-change, classification, approval-operation or first-response authority. Department Head is department-scoped instead (checked separately, against the specific department), not cross-department. Unaffected by the Assign/Transfer correction below — status-change authority was not part of that correction.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketRoleSets.AssignWithinOwnDepartment
member.summary: Assign/reassign, department-scoped (PR correction — explicit task instruction, superseding this file's original Assign design): CS Supervisor and Department Head may assign/reassign only within a department they themselves belong to (checked separately against the ticket's current department). CS Agent and Department Employee hold no assignment capability at all — not even self-claim.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketRoleSets.ReviewEscalations
member.summary: Review of tickets escalated because the handling agent could not resolve them (the escalated queue filter). Supervisory roles only; it narrows the list and never widens visibility — the caller's department scope still applies, so a Department Head reviews only their own department's escalations. member.summary: Transfer (PR correction): CS Manager only. Every other role — including Department Head and CS Supervisor, who retain Assign authority above — is forbidden and must receive 403.

member.summary: Resolve: Department Employee/Head only (ISSUE-022, Management-Decisions.md — ticket task's explicit instruction). Never CS-layer, never cross-department — the resolving actor must also be department-scoped to the ticket's current department.

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketRoleSets.Close
member.summary: Close: CS Agent/CS Supervisor/CS Manager only (ISSUE-022, Management-Decisions.md — task's explicit instruction). Cross-department — CS is inherently cross-department (Security-Architecture.md §3).

member.name: F:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketRoleSets.Reopen
member.summary:
Reopen: the CS layer — CS Agent, CS Supervisor, CS Manager, per the final approved rule. This restores Supervisor and CS Manager, who were briefly excluded while the rule read "the Agent reopens"; management has confirmed the reopening authority is the CS layer as a whole. It is still deliberately not an alias of — the two sets happen to coincide today, and the separation is what lets either move without dragging the other with it (ISSUE-022's Resolve/Close split is the standing example).
System Administrator is absent here and authorized anyway, through ADR-0024's central override, exactly as this class's own summary describes. It is not listed locally: doing so would be the per-call-site duplication that ADR-0024 rules out, and would lose the distinction between what the permission matrix grants and what the override grants on top of it.
Every other role is refused — Department Employee, Department Head, General Manager, Chairman/CEO and Reporting User hold no direct Reopen, neither the action nor the endpoint. They have no direct reopen capability; the Reopen Approval path (ApprovalType.ReopenApproval, which applies to Resolved tickets only, never to an inactivity closure) is the route for a reopen request that CS then decides.
Role membership alone is not authorization for Reopen. Unlike the other sets here, TicketLifecycleAppService.ReopenAsync additionally requires the caller to have access to the ticket itself under the existing visibility rules ( or department membership, via TicketQueryAppService's own check) — the resource-level half of the decision, so a CS user can only reopen a ticket they were entitled to see in the first place.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketVisibilityRule
member.summary:
The one definition of "may this caller see this ticket at all" — Security-Architecture.md §3's rule that access is "evaluated against the ticket's current data, not cached or assumed from the user's session alone". Three kinds of caller:
a CS-layer/executive role ( other than CS Agent: CS Supervisor, CS Manager, General Manager, Chairman/CEO, System Administrator) sees every department;
a CS Agent () sees only the tickets that are assigned to them right now or on which they actually handled a Genesys interaction () — not every ticket, and not every ticket of their department or Genesys queue;
everyone else sees only departments they are actually assigned to.
The two grants a CS Agent has are independent: reassigning the ticket takes away the previous assignee's assignment grant but never their handling grant, and a ticket handled by several agents (a transfer) is visible to each of them. An unassigned ticket nobody handled is visible to no CS Agent.
Extracted from TicketQueryAppService (which still owns the read paths and simply delegates here) when the approved Reopen rule added a resource-level check to a mutation. Two call sites evaluating ticket visibility is fine; two call sites each spelling the rule out is how they drift apart, and a visibility rule that drifts is a disclosure bug. The set-based form of the same rule, for list and aggregate queries, is TicketQueryFilters.VisibleTo; the two must be kept in step.
Routed through , so the ADR-0024 System Administrator override applies here exactly as it does everywhere else — and, as the gate's async overload guarantees, without a department-membership round trip for an overridden caller.

member.summary: True when the caller's ticket visibility is the narrow CS Agent rule: they hold CS Agent and no other role that grants cross-department view (CS Supervisor, CS Manager, General Manager, Chairman/CEO, System Administrator keep the unchanged, unrestricted view — a person who is both Agent and Supervisor is a Supervisor for this purpose).

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketVisibilityRule.IsRestrictedCsAgent(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{System.String},System.Guid,TigerCS.Application.Authorization.IServiceIdentityRegistry)
member.summary: for a known caller: a configured service identity (the Genesys integration account, which Identity models as a "CS Agent" employee) is never restricted. It is not a person who handled anything; it is confined to the integration surface by ServiceIdentityRestrictionHandler and must keep working across tickets there (customer lookups, reconciliation), exactly as before.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Application.Modules.Ticketing.Services.TicketVisibilityRule.HoldsDepartmentRole(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{System.String})
member.summary: A restricted CS Agent who ALSO holds a department role (Department Employee / Head) keeps that role's own department scope — it is granted by the other role, not by CS Agent. CS Agent alone grants nothing by department.

For an operation whose role gate has already passed (Close, Classify, Reopen, request a downgrade…): everyone but a restricted CS Agent passes unchanged — their authority was decided by that role gate — and a restricted CS Agent additionally needs the ticket to be one they may modify (Full access — a creator's read-only access does not count). This is what stops the CS Agent's cross-department action rights reaching tickets they cannot see.
Department-level visibility. A restricted CS Agent has none from CS Agent itself — their access is per ticket (), so this fails closed for them.

How much of a ticket the caller may use. is everything the caller's roles allow on it; is open-and-read only (details, status, owner, department, history, updates) with no modification of any kind; is no access.
For a restricted CS Agent: Full when the ticket is assigned to them, they handled a Genesys interaction on it, or a department role of theirs covers its department; otherwise ReadOnly when they created it — which is how a creator keeps following a ticket after it has moved to another department — otherwise None. Everyone else keeps exactly their department-based answer (Full or None): roles that can see tickets across departments, and department members, are unchanged.
May the caller open and read the ticket — Full or ReadOnly access. Reads (details, history, notes list, SLA, interactions…) use this.

May the caller change the ticket (add a note, close, reopen, classify, claim, assign…): only Full access. A creator who is outside the ticket's department and holds no other grant is ReadOnly and is refused here — the server-side half of "view only", beneath any hidden button.
